sections.title: Papers to check with your employer

groups.title: Cost of living
groups.summary: Rents are asking prices from agency listings (about USD 500-750 for a 1-bed), none dated. Groceries lean on Numbeo, which has few contributors, plus the government maximum-price list. Health is solid: a GP visit is SRD 800-1,600, and the state health fund is SRD 785 a month, paid a year up front by foreigners.

groups.title: Housing and areas
groups.summary: Eleven areas, none labelled safe, because no official source ranks neighbourhoods. Paramaribo-Noord has the most expat housing and the most flooding reports. Rolling power cuts since 25 Aug 2026. Rent law: SRD unless foreign-currency income, 3 months notice, rises capped at inflation. Never pay before an in-person viewing.

groups.title: Money and banking
groups.summary: About 37.5 SRD to the dollar (central bank, 20 Oct). Inflation 8.9% in July 2026. Four banks publish non-resident account lists; none says whether a residence permit is needed. Wise does not serve Suriname residents. Daily life is mostly cash.

groups.title: Phone, internet and transport
groups.summary: Telesur and Digicel; a SIM is about SRD 115, a month of data about SRD 950. Home fibre about SRD 1,125 a month on a 2-year contract. No Uber or Bolt; buses are cash and unscheduled. Airport is 45 km out; book a pickup. Keep the Philippine SIM alive for OTPs.

groups.title: Health, safety and daily life
groups.summary: Canada says normal precautions; the Netherlands says yellow. Chikungunya outbreak from January 2026 still current; malaria-free since 2025. Emergency: 115 police, 113 ambulance, 110 fire. Mostly 127 V power. Manila is 11 hours ahead. No Philippine embassy; Brasilia covers it.

groups.title: Papers (light)
groups.summary: Nine things to confirm with the employer: DMW direct hire, the OEC or OFW Pass, Suriname as a destination, PDOS, OWWA, SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG, apostilles, NAIA departure checks and yellow fever. Several official sites blocked the research, so these need checking on the real pages.

groups.title: Food, places and fun
groups.summary: Ten dishes, nine places, six weekend trips, nine hobbies and festivals, eight pretty-and-cute spots; 22 with freely licensed Wikimedia Commons photos. The Palmentuin may still be closed. Galibi turtle season and Divali fall outside her arrival. No Filipino shop or group confirmed yet.

groups.title: Nomads guide
groups.summary: Read in Chrome: expat month about USD 1,717, local about USD 799, 1-bed in the centre USD 486. Low confidence: 17 reviews from nomads, not residents.

groups.title: Exchange rates
groups.summary: Central bank weighted averages for 20 Oct 2026, plus a mid-market reference for pesos.

openQuestions.q: What is the salary, and in which currency (SRD, USD or EUR)? Gross or net? When is the first payday?
Which office or area will she work in? That unlocks the rent suggestions.
Is temporary housing provided when she lands, and for how long?
Is there an airport pickup? (The airport is 45 km out and taxis have no meter.)
Can she open a local bank account before her residence permit? Will they write the employer letter banks ask for?
Health cover: company insurance, or the state health fund (SZF), which foreigners pay a year up front?
Relocation money: prepaid or reimbursed? Does it cover a rental deposit?
Who handles the Philippine side: DMW direct hire, the OEC or OFW Pass, PDOS?
Can the ticket be multi-city via Toronto, with her paying any difference? And when do they need her passport?
Which Philippine bank cards do you have (Visa or Mastercard)?
Which appliances are you bringing? Most sockets are 127 V.
Have you had the yellow fever shot? If not, the Bureau of Quarantine by about 10 Nov.

toronto.summary: A week in Toronto on the way, to see Bebu. She needs a Canadian visitor visa (TRV): IRCC says about 24 days for the Philippines, so the application has to go in by about 22 Oct to land around 20 Nov. There is no nonstop Toronto to Paramaribo; Caribbean Airlines via Port of Spain is the simplest. Avoid Miami without a US visa.
steps: Apply for the visitor visa online this week (CAD 100 + CAD 85 biometrics).
Book biometrics at VFS Manila or Cebu.
Ask the employer for a multi-city ticket: Manila to Toronto, Toronto to Paramaribo, before they issue it.
Get the yellow fever shot: Port of Spain and Panama are risk countries.
Pack a real coat: Toronto in late November is around freezing.

costs.label: Extra airfare for the Toronto routing
costs.note: Not known until the employer quotes a multi-city ticket. Round trips Toronto-Paramaribo start around CAD 1,055 (Caribbean Airlines, Nov 2026).

costs.label: Winter coat and boots
costs.note: An estimate. Late November in Toronto is near freezing.

costs.label: A week of food and fun
costs.note: Your call. Staying with Bebu, so no hotel.

D5.bus.label: Public bus, airport to Paramaribo
D5.bus.value: SRD 35 per person plus SRD 35 per suitcase. Buses marked 'Zanderij' run from the main terminal between Heiligenweg and Knuffelsgracht. They don't enter the airport: you board on the highway, about a 5-minute walk away. The trip takes just under 2 hours.
D5.bus.notes: Not for arrival day. With luggage, after a 30-hour trip, take a car.
D5.bus.limits: One traveller's paid fare (city to airport direction), matched by an undated guide. There's no timetable and buses leave when full. Other guides say there's no public bus.

conflicts.value: No scheduled public bus; shared minibuses leave when full

D5.distance.label: Airport (PBM, Zanderij) to Paramaribo: distance and drive time
D5.distance.value: About 45 km south of the city (one guide says 55 km). 45-60 minutes by car via the Martin Luther Kingweg, longer at rush hour.
D5.distance.notes: The airport is not in the city: it's about an hour's drive. Don't land late at night without a booked ride.
D5.distance.limits: 45 km is the usual figure. 55 km is probably door to door in the centre.

conflicts.source: Wikipedia / Airport Transfer Portal / Travel With Hello

conflicts.value: 55 km, 'a little over an hour'

D5.shuttle.label: Airport shuttle bus (shared)
D5.shuttle.value: GoVia Airport Express: EUR 15 per person. A taxi on to her door costs EUR 10-15 more. Another guide says a shared bus runs to the Hermitage Mall area in about 1h15.
D5.shuttle.notes: A middle option if no pickup is arranged. Book ahead and check it meets her flight.
D5.shuttle.limits: One undated guide. The shuttle operator's own page wasn't opened, so whether it meets every flight (or only the Amsterdam ones) isn't known.

D5.taxi.label: Taxi or private transfer, airport to Paramaribo
D5.taxi.notes: Budget USD 30-60 for a car to her hotel, and ask the employer or hotel to arrange the pickup (it may be part of her moving package, A3). Agree the price and the currency before getting in.
D5.taxi.limits: There's no meter and no published tariff: the fare is agreed before you set off. The sources disagree widely and mix SRD, USD and EUR. The USD range here covers the quoted USD figures only, and the others are kept under conflicts.

conflicts.value: USD 30-60 sedan, pre-booked; taxis unmetered, negotiate

E1.area.centrum.label: Centrum (historic inner city, Waterkant)
E1.area.centrum.value: Vibe: the UNESCO-listed colonial core and main commercial district, with markets, government offices, most business hotels, cafes and the riverfront Waterkant. Housing: older wooden buildings and apartments; fewer modern units. Commute: shortest of any area if the job is downtown. Walkability: the most walkable part of the city (heat limits distance). Safety evidence: the Palmentuin is named by Canada, the UK and an expat blog for illicit activity, thefts and assaults, especially at night; the Dutch advice warns about streets and parks outside the nightlife area; an expat aggregator calls the centre 'walkable but can be noisy'. Flooding: Starnieuws commentary (May 2026) says the old centre was built on sand ridges about 3 m above sea level, higher than the north, with low hollows between them; drains on Slangenhoutstraat and Calcuttastraat were being rebuilt in Oct 2026 because of water nuisance.
E1.area.centrum.notes: Good if the office is downtown and she wants to walk to things in daylight. At night, taxis rather than walking, and steer clear of the Palmentuin.

sources.publisher: Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs, reisadvies

E1.area.centrum.limits: Neighbourhood descriptions come from expat blogs and an aggregator, not official sources. One listing seen: Beter Wonenstraat 21, furnished 1-bed, EUR 550 (Remy Vastgoed, 2026).

E1.area.commewijne-meerzorg.label: Commewijne side: Meerzorg (across the Jules Wijdenbosch Bridge)
E1.area.commewijne-meerzorg.value: Vibe: Meerzorg (12,405 in 2012) sits on the east bank of the Suriname River directly opposite Paramaribo, a designated suburban and regional centre with housing projects. Commute: across the Jules Wijdenbosch Bridge (opened 2000); an expat blog says daily commuting is realistically by car and public transport is irregular. In October 2026 a parliamentarian said the new school year again brought long queues on the bridge, and raised concerns about heavy trucks and deferred bridge maintenance. Flooding: Commewijne was among the districts hit in May 2026. Safety: no area-specific source.
E1.area.commewijne-meerzorg.notes: Quieter and cheaper, but the bridge is the only road link and it backs up at rush hour. Only worth it if the job is on that side or she has a car.
E1.area.commewijne-meerzorg.limits: No sourced commute time over the bridge. A search result mentioned tap-water problems in Meerzorg but the page was not opened (see gaps).

E1.area.flora.label: Flora (resort, includes Uitvlugt)
E1.area.flora.value: Vibe: a resort of Paramaribo (19,538 people in 2012, about 4 km2, elevation 4 m) described by an expat blog as a developing residential area with new construction; Suriname International School is there. The Zorg en Hoop airfield lies between Zorg en Hoop and Flora. Flooding: a 2002 study suggested Flora A then had relatively little water nuisance after rain (the author hedged it, and it is 24 years old). Safety, commute: no area-specific source.
E1.area.flora.notes: Possible middle-ground area; check the specific street for flooding with neighbours, as for everywhere.
E1.area.flora.limits: The flood note is from 2002. No current area data.

E1.area.kwatta.label: Kwatta (west)
E1.area.kwatta.value: Vibe: quiet, single-storey detached houses with gardens, popular with families and retirees per an expat blog, which says it is relatively far from business centres and that a car is effectively required. Listings seen (2026): furnished house, 120 m2, EUR 750 (Oso Nanga Djari); Thebestraat 7 furnished 4-bed EUR 1,850 (Remy). Flooding, safety: no area-specific source.
E1.area.kwatta.notes: Better with a car. Probably not the first pick for someone new and on her own.

sources.publisher: Oso Nanga Djari Makelaars en Taxateurs (agency listings)

E1.area.kwatta.limits: Single blog source for the vibe.

E1.area.latour-livorno.label: Latour, Livorno and Pontbuiten (south)
E1.area.latour-livorno.value: Vibe: Latour is the most populous resort of Paramaribo (29,526 in 2012); Wikipedia describes it as a low-income neighbourhood with large unemployment. Livorno is described by an expat blog as rapidly developing, with a car recommended. Flooding: a 2002 study named Pontbuiten, Latour and Latour II (Livorno) as the areas with open ditches and the most water problems (88% of surveyed Pontbuiten residents reported flooding) and called the south low-lying. Listing seen: Mackzovereemstraat 27, Livorno, furnished 2-bed EUR 800 (Remy Vastgoed, 2026). Safety: no area-specific official source.
E1.area.latour-livorno.notes: Cheaper, but the older evidence points to more flooding. Look carefully at the street and yard after rain.
E1.area.latour-livorno.limits: The flood study is from 2002; drainage may have changed. No current sourced safety data.

E1.area.leiding.label: Leiding (Wanica)
E1.area.leiding.value: Vibe and housing: semi-rural district area of Wanica, south-west of the city, with houses on larger plots. Listings seen (2026): Soekaredjoweg furnished single-storey house EUR 1,000 (Oso Nanga Djari); Glitterstraat 16 furnished 3-bed EUR 1,500, Indrawatieweg and Matipassi unfurnished EUR 1,500 (Remy). Flooding: Wanica was among the districts hit in the May 2026 rains, and Wanica farmland flooded. Commute, safety: no area-specific source.
E1.area.leiding.notes: Mostly houses, not flats, and far from the centre. Only makes sense if the job turns out to be on that side.

sources.publisher: Oso Nanga Djari Makelaars en Taxateurs (agency listings)

E1.area.leiding.limits: No source described Leiding itself beyond listings; the vibe line is inferred from listings showing large plots, so treat it as weak.

E1.area.lelydorp.label: Lelydorp (Wanica)
E1.area.lelydorp.value: Vibe: Wanica's main town and Suriname's second-largest place (18,663 in 2012), described as a big village with farmland near the centre, on the road between Paramaribo and the international airport at Zanderij. An expat blog calls it semi-rural and relaxed, with houses on big plots and limited specialist healthcare, international schools and Western-style shops; Regional Hospital Wanica is here. Listings seen (2026): furnished upper-floor home EUR 600 (Oso Nanga Djari); Javaweg 22 unfurnished 4-bed EUR 650 (Remy). Flooding: the Ministry of Agriculture (LVV) found drainage channels around Lelydorp with more than 20 years' maintenance backlog and dumped waste blocking flow, raising flood risk for residential areas (Jul and Aug 2026). Scams: a fake-landlord rental scam was reported to Lelydorp police in Dec 2025. Commute: no sourced time; an expat blog says a car is realistic.
E1.area.lelydorp.notes: Cheaper and closer to the international airport, but a commute and fewer services. Not the easy option for a first year alone without a car.

sources.publisher: Oso Nanga Djari Makelaars en Taxateurs (agency listings)

E1.area.lelydorp.limits: No sourced commute time to central Paramaribo.

E1.area.noord.label: Paramaribo-Noord (Rainville, Blauwgrond, Maretraite, Mon Plaisir, Morgenstond, Tourtonne)
E1.area.noord.value: Vibe: the most affluent part of the city and where most expats and diplomats live (Jarnias 2026; Tales Mag 2022); Blauwgrond is a food and nightlife strip; Maretraite and Rainville are quieter and residential; Mon Plaisir is cheaper and newer. Housing: detached houses with gardens, gated compounds (e.g. Green View Lake, Anton Dragten, Sunparklaan) and newer apartment blocks. Commute: an expat blog says reasonable access to main roads; a car is commonly assumed; no sourced times to the centre. Flooding: the north is low (about 1 m above sea level per Starnieuws commentary) and was hit in May 2026 when pumps at Sommelsdijksekreek and Boomskreek failed during power cuts; residents also named Anton Dragtenweg and Jan Steenstraat (Mathoera pump); OWRO cleared drains in Bonistraat, Rubenstraat, Mozartstraat/Anamoestraat, Mylonietstraat and Kasabastraat in April 2026; NOS in 2022 said the north is at extra risk because of its sea-side location and new estates without proper drainage. Safety evidence: an expat blog reports burglaries targeting expat homes here; Starnieuws (Oct 2026) reports burglary gangs cutting fibre lines to disable alarms and cameras citywide. Utilities: SWM's Blauwgrond water station has had low pressure during EBS load-shedding (Oct 2026).
E1.area.noord.notes: Most expat-oriented housing is here, including small gated compounds. It is also the part of town most reported for street flooding. Ask for a raised ground floor or an upper-floor unit, and ask about backup power.
E1.area.noord.limits: Vibe descriptions are from expat blogs and an aggregator; expatlife.ai's pages show signs of automated content (labels misaligned). KW Suriname expat listings here run USD 1,500 to 6,000 for large homes (2026), well above a single person's need.

E1.area.uitvlugt.label: Uitvlugt
E1.area.uitvlugt.value: Vibe: established, green residential area, in Flora resort; Wikipedia calls it a 'wealthy neighbourhood' and two expat sources list it among areas popular with expats. Housing: larger homes with gardens, plus some apartments. Listings seen (2026): Albergastraat 20B furnished 3-bed EUR 1,150; Maystraat 53 furnished 2-bed EUR 1,000; A.G. Ellislaan 23 unfurnished 3-bed EUR 2,200 (Remy Vastgoed). Flooding: a 2002 study singled out 'Uitvlugt 43' for long-lasting flooding. Safety, commute: no area-specific source.
E1.area.uitvlugt.notes: Comfortable, family-ish area, mostly houses rather than small flats, so a 1-bed may be harder to find here.
E1.area.uitvlugt.limits: Flood note is from 2002 and names one sub-area only. Listing prices are asking prices, not signed leases.

E1.area.zorg-en-hoop.label: Zorg en Hoop
E1.area.zorg-en-hoop.value: Vibe: mixed residential area next to Zorg en Hoop airport, a small airfield for light aircraft, helicopters, charters and the Georgetown (Guyana) route; an expat blog says to check aircraft noise. Housing: houses and apartments at various price levels; one agency lists a stone single-storey house there, furnished or unfurnished, EUR 700 (Oso Nanga Djari, 2026); Correa lists a fully air-conditioned rental (Hortensia) in Zorg en Hoop. The Diakonessenhuis hospital is at Zinniastraat 64 (the source does not name the neighbourhood). Commute, flooding and safety: no area-specific source found.
E1.area.zorg-en-hoop.notes: A mid-city option worth a look if the job is in the centre or south-west. Visit at different times to hear the planes, and ask neighbours whether the street floods.

sources.publisher: Oso Nanga Djari Makelaars en Taxateurs (agency listings)

E1.area.zorg-en-hoop.limits: Thin evidence. No sourced commute time, flood record or safety statement for Zorg en Hoop specifically.

E1.area.zuid-hermitage.label: Paramaribo-Zuid / west-central (L'Hermitage, Elisabethshof, Welgelegen, Tammenga)
E1.area.zuid-hermitage.value: Vibe: south Paramaribo is described as more commercial and local, with markets, traffic and shopping centres such as Hermitage Mall; Uitvlugt is the quieter pocket. Listings seen (2026): Elisabethshof furnished 2-bed EUR 650, unfurnished 2-bed EUR 500 (Remy Vastgoed); Tammenga apartment for singles or couples EUR 650 (Oso Nanga Djari); L'Hermitage furnished houses EUR 1,350 to 2,100 (Remy). Correa lists apartments near Hermitage Mall with alarms or cameras. Flooding, safety, commute: no area-specific source.
E1.area.zuid-hermitage.notes: Has more modest-sized flats than the north, near shopping. Worth including in a viewing trip.

sources.publisher: Oso Nanga Djari Makelaars en Taxateurs (agency listings)

E1.area.zuid-hermitage.limits: Listing prices are asking prices; no sourced flood or safety data for these neighbourhoods.

E1.overview.hospitals.label: Hospitals in Greater Paramaribo (to judge closeness from an area)
E1.overview.hospitals.value: Academisch Ziekenhuis Paramaribo (AZP) is the country's largest hospital (465 beds). 's Lands Hospitaal is at Tourtonnelaan 3. The Diakonessenhuis is at Zinniastraat 64. Sint Vincentius Ziekenhuis is in Paramaribo. Regional Hospital Wanica opened in Lelydorp on 7 Feb 2020.
E1.overview.hospitals.notes: When shortlisting a flat, check the drive to the nearest of these, and ask the employer's HR which hospital their health insurance uses.
E1.overview.hospitals.limits: Exact neighbourhood of each hospital and the location of AZP's emergency department were not confirmed from an opened source. No source mapped GP clinics or supermarkets by neighbourhood.

E1.overview.safety-evidence.label: What the evidence says about safety across Greater Paramaribo
E1.overview.safety-evidence.value: No government source ranks Paramaribo neighbourhoods by safety. Canada (13 Oct 2026) and the UK say petty crime is common and violent crime (armed robbery, burglary, carjacking) occurs particularly in Paramaribo and surrounding areas, with pickpocketing and robbery around business and shopping areas and hotels. The only spot every source names inside the city is the Palmentuin (Palm Garden) in the centre. The Netherlands (16 Oct 2026) advises caution in streets and parks outside the nightlife area and notes criminals often carry firearms or machetes. Belgium (8 Sep 2026) says the hotel district is considered relatively safe and advises avoiding non-tourist neighbourhoods and evening and night walking alone. An April 2026 expat blog says no neighbourhood is free of crime and reports burglaries in the affluent north targeting expat homes believed to keep cash.
E1.overview.safety-evidence.notes: Treat every area below as 'no specific warning found', not 'safe'. Choose a home with a fenced yard and a locking gate, use taxis after dark, and don't keep much cash at home.

sources.publisher: Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs, reisadvies

E1.overview.safety-evidence.limits: The US State Department and OSAC pages could not be opened (HTTP 403). No neighbourhood-level police statistics were found that could be opened.

E2.rent.1bed.centre.numbeo.label: Rent, 1-bedroom, city centre (Numbeo)
E2.rent.1bed.centre.numbeo.notes: Crowd-sourced average. Treat as a rough check on the agent listings, not as a price.
E2.rent.1bed.centre.numbeo.limits: The whole Paramaribo page rests on 64 entries from 6 contributors in 12 months, spread over every item. Furnished status not specified. At the roughly 37.7-37.9 SRD/USD that Numbeo and Rio Times imply, the typical is about USD 485.

E2.rent.1bed.listings.label: Rent, 1-bedroom apartment, Paramaribo (agent listings, furnishing mostly not stated)
E2.rent.1bed.listings.notes: Plan on roughly USD 500-750 for an ordinary 1-bedroom from an agent. The cheapest listings tend to be gone already.
E2.rent.1bed.listings.limits: Six 1-bed listings priced in USD: 300 (rented), 500, 650, 735, 1,000 (rented), plus one at EUR 450 (rented) and one 'price upon request' in the centre. Several are already let. Furnishing is not stated. No listing dates.

conflicts.value: USD 400-555 (central, unfurnished); USD 200-350 (suburbs, unfurnished)
conflicts.scope: Paramaribo; unsourced estimate, says only 'Numbeo 2025' as background

E2.rent.1bed.outside.numbeo.label: Rent, 1-bedroom, outside the centre (Numbeo)
E2.rent.1bed.outside.numbeo.notes: Cheaper places exist outside the centre, but they are usually found by word of mouth, not through agents.
E2.rent.1bed.outside.numbeo.limits: Same thin Numbeo sample (64 entries, 6 contributors, all items). About USD 265 at ~37.8 SRD/USD, which is below every 1-bed agent listing we found.

conflicts.value: USD 500-735 for available 1-beds

E2.rent.2bed.listings.usd.label: Rent, 2-bedroom apartment, Paramaribo (agent listings in USD)
E2.rent.2bed.listings.usd.notes: Two bedrooms is where prices spread out most. Newer complexes in the north and south go well above USD 1,000.
E2.rent.2bed.listings.usd.limits: Keller Williams 2-beds in USD run 600-1,850, clustering around 800-1,250. Many are already rented. Surgoed's 'Appartement' listings (bedrooms not stated, 90-100 m²) are USD 900-1,500. No dates, and furnishing is mostly not stated.

E2.rent.furnished.estimate.label: Rent, furnished 1-bedroom with AC (estimate)
E2.rent.furnished.estimate.notes: Furnished costs more. Plan on USD 600-900 for a decent furnished 1-bed with AC, and check every quote against a real listing.
E2.rent.furnished.estimate.scope: Paramaribo: Uitvlugt/Zorg en Hoop 450-750, Noord 550-950, Combé and inner city 600-1,000
E2.rent.furnished.estimate.limits: Neither source cites where its prices come from. Expatlife.ai gives USD 600-900 for a 'furnished expat apartment', with a 'verified' date that matches the day we read it, so it may be auto-stamped. Travel And Tour World gives USD 500-900 overall.

conflicts.value: EUR 800-999 for the cheaper furnished long-stay homes (1-3 bedrooms), EUR 1,500-2,500 for the rest, on leases over 3 months

E2.rent.studio.listings.label: Rent, studio, Paramaribo (agent listings)
E2.rent.studio.listings.notes: Studios do exist at USD 300-400 a month in Paramaribo-Noord, but we only found one building's worth of them.
E2.rent.studio.listings.scope: Paramaribo-Noord (one building, Houtbijstraat 37: small / medium / large studios)
E2.rent.studio.listings.limits: All three studios are in one building, so this is one landlord's pricing, not a market range. Listing dates and furnished status are not shown. No other agent site listed studios.

E3.agents.label: Agents (makelaars) and who pays them
E3.agents.value: Several agencies list rentals online with prices and photos: Keller Williams Suriname (with an 'expat homes' page), RE/MAX Suriname, Surgoed, Oso Nanga Djari, Remy Vastgoed, EasyRent and Correa (which also manages properties for owners). Surgoed charges its fee, one month's rent, to the owner when a lease is signed (no cure, no pay).
E3.agents.notes: Ask any agent in writing, before viewings, whether she pays a fee. Going through an established agency lowers the fake-landlord risk.

sources.publisher: Oso Nanga Djari Makelaars en Taxateurs (agency listings)

E3.agents.limits: Only one agency's fee terms were read. Whether tenants pay a fee elsewhere was not confirmed. No official register of licensed agents was found.

E3.deposit.label: Security deposit norm
E3.deposit.value: EasyRent says long stays need a deposit, often 1 to 2 months' rent, stated in the lease. The rental law sets no deposit rule or cap.
E3.deposit.notes: Budget for the first month plus one to two months' deposit at signing, and get a receipt and an inventory with photos.

sources.publisher: De Nationale Assemblee (Staatsblad 2020 no. 53, Huurwet Woonruimte 2020)

E3.deposit.limits: One agency's statement; no independent survey of deposits found.

E3.foreigner-docs.label: What landlords ask foreigners for
E3.foreigner-docs.value: No source that could be opened lists what landlords require from foreign tenants. Surgoed says only that it applies 'some conditions' to screen tenants. EasyRent says it helps long-stay tenants with registration in Suriname.
E3.foreigner-docs.notes: Expect to show a passport and the job offer or contract. Ask the agency for their list in writing.
E3.foreigner-docs.limits: Gap. Search snippets from secondary guides mention passport, permit and proof of income, but those pages were not opened.

E3.law.currency.label: Rent currency: SRD by law, foreign currency allowed for some tenants
E3.law.currency.value: Article 13 of the Huurwet Woonruimte 2020 says rent is set in Surinamese dollars (SRD), but rent may be set in a foreign currency when the tenant is not a resident, or is a resident with a demonstrable fixed income in a foreign currency. The law's explanatory note says pricing rents in USD or EUR had become common. In practice the agency listings seen in 2026 quote in EUR or USD.
E3.law.currency.notes: If her salary is in SRD, she can ask for rent in SRD. If it is in USD or EUR, expect the rent in that currency. Check A2 (salary currency) first.

sources.publisher: De Nationale Assemblee (Staatsblad 2020 no. 53, Huurwet Woonruimte 2020)
Oso Nanga Djari Makelaars en Taxateurs (agency listings)

E3.law.currency.limits: How courts treat a newcomer with an SRD salary paying in EUR was not researched.

E3.lease-length.label: Typical lease length
E3.lease-length.value: Agencies aimed at expats offer long stays from 3 months up to 2 years (EasyRent) or from 3 months (Correa); some Correa listings require a minimum of one year. Surgoed's fee example refers to a one-year contract. Shorter furnished stays (from 5 or 7 nights) are run as holiday rentals, which the rental law does not cover.
E3.lease-length.notes: A 3-month furnished lease from an agency is a realistic bridge after temporary housing, then a 12-month lease once she knows the area.

sources.publisher: De Nationale Assemblee (Staatsblad 2020 no. 53, Huurwet Woonruimte 2020)

E3.lease-length.limits: Agency pages only; private landlords may differ.

E3.remote.label: Renting from abroad before arrival
E3.remote.value: Expat guides advise against signing a long lease before seeing the property and suggest starting in a short furnished stay, then viewing neighbourhoods in person at different times of day. An April 2026 blog recommends an agency that works with expats because the market is small.
E3.remote.notes: Plan: employer temp housing or a short furnished stay (E4) for the first weeks, view in person, then sign.
E3.remote.limits: Advice from expat guides, not data.

E3.scams.label: Rental scams
E3.scams.value: Police have arrested fake landlords more than once: in Wanica (Dec 2025) a man posed as an apartment owner, took rent and disappeared; in Wanica (Apr 2021) a woman showed 11 people homes that weren't hers, took advance rent and stopped answering when they asked for keys. Police also warn (Jun 2026) about Facebook offers where the buyer pays an advance to a bank account and the seller then blocks them; that warning was about goods, but the pattern matches.
E3.scams.notes: Never pay before seeing the place in person (or having a trusted person see it) and checking that the person is the owner or a real agency. Pay to a business account against a written lease. If scammed, report at the nearest police station with screenshots and the bank account number.
E3.scams.limits: Few reports, and police don't publish totals. No report specifically about scams aimed at foreigners renting from abroad was found.

E4.shortstay.vacation-rental.nightly.label: Short stay, vacation rental apartments, nightly (Momondo)
E4.shortstay.vacation-rental.nightly.notes: A simple furnished apartment runs from about USD 25 to USD 75 a night. For 2-4 weeks, ask for a weekly or monthly rate. Her employer may be covering this anyway.
E4.shortstay.vacation-rental.nightly.limits: The page shows '$' without a currency code (it is the US site). No dates were chosen, so these are 'from' prices. Cleaning fees and taxes are not shown.

conflicts.value: Average USD 64/night on a 7-day stay; 'typical' USD 73/night; range USD 20-93
conflicts.scope: Momondo's own summary figures on the same page, undated

E5.ac.label: Air conditioning
E5.ac.value: AC is common in rentals aimed at expats but often only in some rooms: Correa lists some homes as fully air-conditioned and others with AC in one or two bedrooms or only the living room. EasyRent says most, not all, of its homes have AC. An expat guide warns AC raises electricity bills and suggests inverter units or limiting use.
E5.ac.notes: Ask which rooms have AC and whether the units are inverter types. At least the bedroom should have one.

E5.backup-power.label: Power cuts and backup power (load-shedding since Aug 2026)
E5.backup-power.value: Since 25 Aug 2026 the power company EBS has been switching areas off in rotation for at least 3 hours at a time across Paramaribo, Wanica, Commewijne, Para and Saramacca, because demand outgrew supply and there is no reserve. EBS cannot say in advance which areas go off. On 30 Sep 2026 the President promised investment, and Staatsolie plans 34 MW of new generators, with no delivery date. In mid-October cuts at SWM's Blauwgrond station caused low water pressure in Paramaribo-Noord. An expat guide advises asking landlords about backup generator power.
E5.backup-power.notes: This is the live issue for November 2026. Ask every landlord: is there a generator or inverter/battery backup, what does it run (fridge, a fan, Wi-Fi, AC?), and does the building have a water tank and pump? A power bank and a rechargeable fan are worth packing.
E5.backup-power.limits: How often a given neighbourhood loses power was not found. The situation may change by her arrival.

E5.furnished.label: What 'furnished' (gemeubileerd) usually includes
E5.furnished.value: EasyRent's furnished long-stay homes include a bed, wardrobes, sofa, dining table, and a kitchen with fridge and cooking facilities; air conditioning and Wi-Fi are in most but not all; a washing machine in many or on request; final cleaning included. Correa listings vary: some are 'fully furnished', one adds weekly cleaning and Wi-Fi. Agency listings mark furnished and unfurnished separately, and some homes are offered either way.
E5.furnished.notes: Ask for an item-by-item inventory: bed, fridge, stove, washing machine, AC units (which rooms), water heater, Wi-Fi, curtains, kitchenware.

sources.publisher: Oso Nanga Djari Makelaars en Taxateurs (agency listings)

E5.furnished.limits: Agency definitions; a private landlord's 'furnished' may mean less. Linens, kitchenware and TV were not confirmed.

E5.water-heater.label: Hot water
E5.water-heater.value: EasyRent lists 'warm water' as a feature on many of its homes but not as standard in its furnished package, which suggests not every rental has a water heater.
E5.water-heater.notes: Ask directly: is there hot water in the shower?
E5.water-heater.limits: Inference from one agency's listing format. No source states how common water heaters are.

E6.utilities.combined.label: Basic utilities (electricity, cooling, water, garbage) for an 85 m² apartment
E6.utilities.combined.notes: Around SRD 1,400 a month for power and water, which matches our tariff-based calculation for electricity.
E6.utilities.combined.limits: Thin Numbeo sample (64 entries, 6 contributors, all items). 85 m² is bigger than a 1-bed for one person.

conflicts.value: USD 100-170 a month for electricity, water and internet together
conflicts.scope: Unsourced estimate; it includes internet, Numbeo does not

E7.alarm-defeat.label: Alarms that depend on internet can be cut
E7.alarm-defeat.value: Starnieuws (2 Oct 2026) reports police saying burglary gangs cut fibre-optic cables before break-ins to disable internet-connected cameras and alarms; seven suspects were arrested.
E7.alarm-defeat.notes: An alarm with a battery and a mobile (SIM) backup is better than one that only uses Wi-Fi, especially with power cuts on.

E7.bars-fire.label: Bars are a fire trap if there is no way out
E7.bars-fire.value: In 2016 Suriname's Justice Minister warned that burglar-proofed homes were deadly in fires: 13 people had died that year trapped behind interior-fixed iron grilles. Smoke detectors and emergency exits were advised.
E7.bars-fire.notes: Check that the bars have an opening grille or door with a key she keeps near the bed, and buy a smoke alarm.

E7.norms.label: Home security norms
E7.norms.value: Expat-oriented rentals advertise fences, secured gates, alarms and cameras, and gated compounds with 24-hour or semi-gated security (Correa, EasyRent, an Oso Nanga Djari gated community in Rainville). EasyRent says many, not all, of its homes have a fenced yard, secured gate or cameras. An April 2026 expat blog says burglaries are not uncommon and police lack resources, and recommends bars on windows and doors, good locks, a fenced yard with a locking gate, an alarm and cameras, and motion lights; it says homes or streets in the most affluent areas are often guarded by private guards.
E7.norms.notes: Look for: a fence and locking gate, bars or grilles, solid doors, outside lights, and ideally a compound or apartment building with other people around.

sources.publisher: Oso Nanga Djari Makelaars en Taxateurs (agency listings)

E7.norms.limits: No official guidance on home security. The blog is one writer.

E8.centrum-south.label: Flood risk: centre and south
E8.centrum-south.value: Centre: Starnieuws commentary says the old centre was built on higher sand ridges (Hogestraat, Gravenstraat, Kwattaweg) with low hollows between. Work on drains at Slangenhoutstraat and Calcuttastraat (Oct 2026) is part of a 20-month rehabilitation of Van 't Hogerhuysstraat. South: a 2002 study named Pontbuiten, Latour, Latour II (Livorno), parts of Uitvlugt and Hanna's Lust as the worst for flooding, with south Paramaribo low-lying and open ditches overflowing.
E8.centrum-south.notes: Older southern areas with open ditches have a long flood history. Ask neighbours.
E8.centrum-south.limits: The south evidence is from 2002. No recent area survey found.

E8.noord.label: Flood risk: Paramaribo-Noord
E8.noord.value: Repeatedly reported: NOS (2022) said the north is especially at risk because of its sea-side location, low streets and new estates without drainage; the Public Works ministry cleared drains on Bonistraat, Rubenstraat, Mozartstraat/Anamoestraat, Mylonietstraat and Kasabastraat in April 2026; the north was flooded again in May 2026.
E8.noord.notes: The north is where most expat housing is and where flooding is most reported. Check the specific street.

E8.wanica.label: Flood risk: Wanica (Lelydorp, Leiding)
E8.wanica.value: Wanica was among the districts flooded in May 2026 and its farmland stayed waterlogged. In July and August 2026 LVV found drains around Lelydorp blocked by dumped waste and some channels unmaintained for over 20 years, and started clearing about 70 to 80% of the main waterways.
E8.wanica.notes: Lower-lying outer areas may flood; ask about the specific road.
E8.wanica.limits: Mostly agricultural drainage reporting; no list of flooded residential streets.

E8.why.label: Why Paramaribo streets flood
E8.why.value: Paramaribo is low coastal land with a very slight slope; around the Onafhankelijkheidsplein it is about 3 m above mean sea level and parts of the north about 1 m. Drainage runs by gravity and is blocked at high tide. Canals are silted or too few, low areas were built on without planning, and pump stations fail: in May 2026 pumps stopped during EBS power cuts, inlets were clogged, and old sluices were stuck. The government set up a crisis committee on 11 May 2026 and set up a hotline, 844-2646, for serious flooding.
E8.why.notes: Flooding is street-by-street. Power cuts make it worse because pumps stop. Higher ground and upper floors are safer.
E8.why.limits: Causes as reported by government and press, May 2026.

F1.currency.srd.label: Suriname's currency and how it is managed
F1.currency.srd.value: The Surinamese dollar (SRD) is the only legal tender. It floats: the IMF asks the central bank to keep the rate flexible and step in only when markets are disorderly. The US dollar is not legal tender and a shop may refuse it.
F1.currency.srd.notes: Everyday prices are in SRD. Treat the SRD as the money you spend and USD or EUR as the money you save or bring in.
F1.currency.srd.limits: The 'not legal tender, shops may refuse USD' point comes from the Rio Times, not from a central bank page. The CBvS website (cbvs.sr) refused automated access (HTTP 403), so no CBvS page was read directly.

F1.inflation.latest.label: Inflation, latest official reading (July 2026)
F1.inflation.latest.value: 8.9% year on year (July 2026 vs July 2025); prices rose 0.5% from June to July 2026. Provisional.
F1.inflation.latest.notes: Prices are still rising about 9% a year. A salary fixed in SRD loses buying power over a year unless it is adjusted; one in USD or EUR does not, in SRD terms, as long as the rate holds.
F1.inflation.latest.scope: Suriname CPI (Paramaribo, Wanica and districts, ~630 price points)

sources.publisher: Algemeen Bureau voor de Statistiek (ABS), Suriname

F1.inflation.latest.limits: Provisional figures. August and September 2026 readings were not found. The CBvS's own inflation bulletin could not be opened (HTTP 403); search snippets of its April 2026 bulletin put 12-month inflation at 10.9%, which was not verified.

F1.usd.eur.dailyuse.label: How USD and EUR are used day to day
F1.usd.eur.dailyuse.value: Heavily dollarised: 72.5% of bank deposits were in foreign currency in July 2026. Landlords often quote rent in USD, and tours and interior transport are often priced in USD or EUR. Groceries, taxis, markets and small shops work in SRD cash.
F1.usd.eur.dailyuse.notes: Expect to see USD on rent and big-ticket prices, and SRD everywhere else.
F1.usd.eur.dailyuse.limits: The 72.5% deposit figure is quoted by the Rio Times from central-bank data; the CBvS page itself was not opened. 'Often quoted in USD' is descriptive, with no count.

F2.cbvs.eur.label: Official weighted average rate, EUR to SRD
F2.cbvs.eur.value: Transfers: buy 41.807 / sell 42.772. Cash: buy 41.377 / sell 41.994.

F2.cbvs.usd.label: Official weighted average rate, USD to SRD
F2.cbvs.usd.value: Transfers: buy 37.393 / sell 37.930. Cash: buy 37.472 / sell 37.561.
F2.cbvs.usd.limits: A weighted average across banks; individual banks and cambios differ slightly.

F2.php.reference.label: USD to PHP reference rate
F2.php.reference.limits: A mid-market reference; banks and remittance services give less.

F2.rate.cambio.label: Cambio (exchange office) rates, indicative only
F2.rate.cambio.value: A rates board (koers.sr) showed USD buy 37.35 / sell 37.65 and EUR buy 42.20 / sell 43.00, labelled 'updated today' with no date and '0 banks involved'.
F2.rate.cambio.notes: The Rio Times reports that official and market rates converged by mid-2026. Unlike the 2020–2022 crisis, there is no big gap to chase. Change money only at a bank or a CBvS-licensed cambio, never on the street.
F2.rate.cambio.limits: Undated and unattributed; a search index flagged the same page as years old. No licensed cambio's own rate page was read. Not dependable. Use it only to see that cambio and bank rates are now in the same range.

F2.rate.usd.banks.label: USD → SRD at the banks (indicative buy and sell, mid-October 2026)
F2.rate.usd.banks.value: Banks buy USD at 37.15–37.40 and sell at 37.907–37.91. Hakrinbank (20 Oct): buy 37.40 / sell 37.91. Finabank (20 Oct, non-cash): 37.400 / 37.907. DSB (16 Oct, 14:30): 37.15 / 37.91.
F2.rate.usd.banks.notes: Roughly 37–38 SRD to the US dollar. When she sells USD she gets the lower 'buy' number.
F2.rate.usd.banks.limits: Indicative board rates. The bank sets the actual rate at the moment of the transaction. Finabank's sell rate applies only when it has the currency in stock. Cash and non-cash rates can differ.

F3.bank.dsb.label: De Surinaamsche Bank (DSB): opening a giro (current) account
F3.bank.dsb.value: Residents: valid ID (ID card, passport or driving licence), email and mobile number, employer statement. Non-residents: valid passport plus a second ID from home or a PSA document, a reference letter, a proof-of-assets form, an employer statement, a municipal extract as proof of address, email and mobile. Accounts in SRD, USD or EUR. Monthly fee: SRD 25 (SRD account), USD 3 or EUR 3. A first deposit must be made within one month. The online 'Instaprekening' is for residents with a Surinamese e-ID only.
F3.bank.dsb.notes: DSB asks for the most paperwork from non-residents.
F3.bank.dsb.limits: No mention of residence permits. The municipal extract (proof of address) may be hard to get before she is registered, which may make the non-resident list harder in practice than it looks.

F3.bank.finabank.label: Finabank: opening a giro or savings account
F3.bank.finabank.value: Residents: valid ID and first deposit. Non-residents: valid ID (a passport for a savings account), proof of income (salary slip or employer statement), a reference letter or recent statement from the home bank, and a first deposit. A savings account needs an existing Finabank giro account. Opening is by appointment.
F3.bank.finabank.limits: No mention of residence permits. First-deposit amounts were not on the page; the Rio Times reports SRD/USD/EUR 200 for non-resident savings accounts (not verified on Finabank's site).

F3.bank.hakrinbank.label: Hakrinbank: opening a personal account
F3.bank.hakrinbank.value: Documents: signed application form; valid ID (a passport is accepted); an employer statement showing the employer's KKF (Chamber of Commerce) number, no older than one month, or other proof of income. Non-residents must also bring a reference from their foreign bank. Accounts can be in SRD, USD or EUR. Opening is free; foreign-currency accounts need a first deposit of 100 (USD or EUR).
F3.bank.hakrinbank.notes: Bring a reference letter from her Philippine bank. It is the item most likely to hold her up.
F3.bank.hakrinbank.limits: The page does not mention residence permits, or say when a newcomer counts as a resident.

F3.bank.republic.label: Republic Bank Suriname: opening an account
F3.bank.republic.value: Foreign Savings Account (USD/EUR), non-residents: two forms of ID, a foreign bank reference letter or statements under 6 months old, proof of income (employer declaration under 1 month old, or recent salary slips), and proof of address (population-register extract or a utility bill under 3 months old). The Basic SRD Account is for Suriname residents only (income up to SRD 123,000 a year, first deposit SRD 50). Accounts can also be started online at republiconboard.com.
F3.bank.republic.notes: Republic is also the bank whose ATMs most reliably take foreign cards (see F4).
F3.bank.republic.limits: The page contradicts itself on the minimum opening deposit (see conflicts). It does not say what proves 'resident' status, and does not mention permits.

conflicts.value: USD/EUR 50 minimum opening deposit
conflicts.source: Republic Foreign Savings Account page, product highlights

conflicts.value: USD/EUR 100 minimum opening deposit
conflicts.source: Republic Foreign Savings Account page, requirements section

F3.permit.before.account.label: Can she open an account before her residence permit?
F3.permit.before.account.value: Unclear. None of the four banks' pages (Hakrinbank, DSB, Finabank, Republic) mentions a residence permit. All four have a non-resident route, which needs a passport, a reference from her Philippine bank, an employer statement and, at DSB and Republic, proof of a local address. The Rio Times (Sep 2026) also found no stated permit requirement, but suggests it is easier once the permit arrives. Each bank decides case by case.
F3.permit.before.account.notes: Ask HR before she flies. Before leaving the Philippines, get a bank reference letter (in English) and recent statements from her Philippine bank.
F3.permit.before.account.limits: This is an absence of evidence, not a confirmed rule. Southern Commercial Bank's requirements were not found at all. Confirm with the bank her employer uses for payroll, and ask HR which bank other foreign staff use.

F4.atm.foreign.cards.label: Which Suriname ATMs take a foreign Visa or Mastercard
F4.atm.foreign.cards.value: Republic Bank: Visa and Mastercard (daily limit SRD 20,000). DSB: Mastercard and most foreign cards (SRD 10,000). Finabank: Mastercard only (SRD 3,000). Hakrinbank, VCB, SPSB and GODO: local cards only. Most ATMs pay out SRD only.
F4.atm.foreign.cards.notes: Plan B is a Republic Bank ATM, in daylight. Carry two cards from different Philippine banks, one Visa and one Mastercard.

sources.publisher: Tales from a Small Planet (expat post reports)

F4.atm.foreign.cards.limits: Not confirmed on the banks' own pages. Philippine cards were not tested specifically; acceptance also depends on her issuing bank. A forum report says DSB may destroy a swallowed foreign card. The SRD 20,000 limit for Republic matches its own fee manual.

conflicts.value: Most local ATMs reject international cards
conflicts.source: Tales from a Small Planet post report

conflicts.value: Republic and DSB ATMs accept foreign cards

F4.ph.bpi.fees.label: BPI debit card used abroad: fees
F4.ph.bpi.fees.value: International ATM withdrawal: USD 3.50 or 1.75%, whichever is higher. Balance inquiry USD 1.00; declined withdrawal USD 1.00. FX mark-up: +1% over BPI's selling rate. International in-store purchases: 1.5%. International access is on by default and can be switched on or off, with limits set, in the app's Card Control.
F4.ph.bpi.fees.notes: From a BPI card, a withdrawal of SRD 4,000 (about USD 106) costs roughly USD 3.50 at BPI, plus about 1% FX, plus the Suriname ATM fee.
F4.ph.bpi.fees.limits: The page carries no effective date. Card Control details come from search snippets of BPI's own page, which was not opened. The foreign ATM's own fee comes on top. Fees for BDO, Metrobank, UnionBank and other banks were not verified (see gaps).

F5.cash.card.culture.label: Cash vs card in Paramaribo
F5.cash.card.culture.value: Largely cash-based. Cards are taken at major hotels, larger supermarkets, some restaurants and tour operators; some add a card surcharge. Taxis, buses, markets, small shops and restaurants are cash only. Carry small SRD notes, because vendors often lack change.
F5.cash.card.culture.notes: Cash is king in week one.

sources.publisher: Tales from a Small Planet (expat post reports)

F5.cash.card.culture.limits: Travel and expat reports, partly from 2022. Card use is probably growing; no payment-statistics source was found.

F5.cash.which.currency.label: Arrival cash: USD or EUR
F5.cash.which.currency.value: Both USD and EUR are the main currencies exchanged at banks and cambios, and both get a posted rate (see F2). Notes must be clean and undamaged; worn USD notes are often refused. Stay well under the USD 10,000 cross-border limit (see F9).
F5.cash.which.currency.notes: Either currency works. USD is the more common one for rent and big prices.
F5.cash.which.currency.limits: No source gives a recommended amount for a newly arrived employee (see gaps). The USD-vs-EUR choice depends on her route: USD is easier to buy in Manila, EUR if she transits Amsterdam.

F6.bank.wire.republic.label: International bank wire from a Suriname account (Republic Bank tariffs)
F6.bank.wire.republic.value: Outgoing international wire: 0.5% commission (minimum USD/EUR 16.50 incl. VAT) plus USD/EUR 8.25 SWIFT charge (incl. VAT). On a USD 500 transfer, that comes to USD 24.75 at Republic. Incoming international wire: 0.25%, minimum USD 5.50, maximum USD 55 (incl. VAT). A recall or amendment for a client error costs USD 33.
F6.bank.wire.republic.notes: Expect at least about USD 25 per wire, plus deductions along the way. Send a small test transfer first.

sources.publisher: Republic Bank (Suriname) N.V., Fees & Charges v2026.1

F6.bank.wire.republic.limits: The bank's fee only. Correspondent (intermediary) bank charges and the receiving Philippine bank's fees are extra and not known. The Rio Times notes that correspondent banks can slow or reject transfers, and that banks may ask for source-of-funds paperwork on large amounts. Other banks' wire tariffs were not read. 'high' is left null because the total depends on deductions along the way.

F6.western.union.label: Western Union in Suriname
F6.western.union.value: IMT (International Money Transfer, Cirkel Group) is an official Western Union agent, with offices at Wilhelminastraat 64A, Jaggernath Lachmonstraat 26, Qmall (Kwattaweg 223) and Central Mall (Maagdenstraat 54), plus sub-agents. Western Union runs a Suriname site (westernunion.com/sr).
F6.western.union.notes: Likely the easiest walk-in option. Fees and exchange margin are unknown until she asks for a quote.
F6.western.union.limits: Neither page confirms that sending FROM Suriname TO the Philippines is offered, or gives fees, limits or the currency of payment. Visit IMT in person with a passport and ask for a quote.

F6.wise.label: Wise: can she use it from Suriname?
F6.wise.value: Probably not as a Suriname resident. Suriname is not on Wise's list of countries where you can live and hold money with Wise. Sending INTO Suriname in SRD is offered from some countries (e.g. Canada), although Wise's help page leaves Suriname off its send-to list.
F6.wise.notes: Don't plan on Wise for sending money home from Suriname.
F6.wise.limits: Wise's own pages disagree about sending to Suriname (see conflicts). Whether a Wise account opened in the Philippines can be kept after a move was not checked. Wise's terms generally require an up-to-date residential address.

conflicts.value: Suriname not on the list of countries you can send to (possible only to USD/EUR/GBP accounts)
conflicts.source: Wise help: what countries can I send to

conflicts.value: CAD → SRD payouts to local bank accounts offered

F7.mope.label: Mopé (Hakrinbank mobile wallet)
F7.mope.value: A phone-number wallet owned by Hakrinbank. It pays by QR code or payment request, cash can be topped up at merchants, credit can be moved to your own bank account, and it pays SWM (water) bills. A Mopé debit card is available.
F7.mope.notes: Useful once she has a local SIM and bank account. Not a substitute for cash in week one.
F7.mope.limits: Sign-up requirements (Surinamese ID? local SIM?) were not stated. How widely shops accept it is unknown. 27 ratings, average 3.9.

F8.wage.tax.brackets.label: Wage tax (loonbelasting): rates and brackets
F8.wage.tax.brackets.value: First SRD 9,000 a month (SRD 108,000 a year) is tax-free. On the rest: 8% up to SRD 3,500 a month; 18% from 3,500 to 7,000; 28% from 7,000 to 10,500; 38% above 10,500 (annual: 42,000 / 84,000 / 126,000). Before this, a flat expense deduction of 4% of gross, capped at SRD 400 a month (SRD 4,800 a year). The top rate is 38%.
F8.wage.tax.brackets.notes: Worked example from the calculator site: a gross SRD 20,000 a month gives about SRD 1,934 wage tax, before AOV pension contributions. A USD or EUR salary is presumably taxed on its SRD value; ask her employer's payroll.
F8.wage.tax.brackets.unit: SRD per month (brackets apply to income above the tax-free sum)
F8.wage.tax.brackets.limits: There was no PwC/Big-4 summary for Suriname (the PwC URLs return 404), and the Belastingdienst page was not read. The thresholds come from a private calculator site and match the January 2024 State Decree as reported by the VSB (tax-free SRD 9,000/month, SRD 3,500 bracket widths, expense deduction SRD 4,800/year). Changes after July 2025 were not ruled out.

F8.withholding.and.bonus.label: Who withholds the tax, and the bonus exemption
F8.withholding.and.bonus.value: Wage tax is withheld by the employer through payroll (the HBN note tells employers to update their payroll for the changes). Holiday pay, bonuses and gratuities are tax-free up to SRD 19,500 a year (raised from SRD 10,016 by State Decree of 22 Jul 2025, retroactive to 1 Jan 2025). Overtime has its own, lighter brackets from 1 Jul 2025.
F8.withholding.and.bonus.notes: She should not need to file anything herself if salary is her only income, but she should ask HR to confirm.
F8.withholding.and.bonus.limits: Whether a salary-only employee owes any further income tax, and how AOV (old-age pension) premiums are withheld, were seen only in search snippets and are listed in the gaps. The AOV rate is not verified (see gaps). Not tax advice: confirm with her employer's payroll or the Belastingdienst Suriname.

F9.bank.fx.limits.label: Bank limits on buying foreign currency and sending it out
F9.bank.fx.limits.value: In November 2024, DSB capped personal purchases of foreign currency at USD 5,000 or EUR 5,000 a month (down from USD 10,000), and Southern Commercial Bank stopped SRD→USD conversion on its UnionPay prepaid cards because of a dollar shortage. Banks may ask for written source-of-funds information on large transfers, and foreign companies need Foreign Exchange Commission approval.
F9.bank.fx.limits.notes: Rules have tightened in shortages before. If she is paid in SRD and wants to send USD home, ask her bank about current monthly limits. A USD or EUR salary avoids having to buy dollars at all.
F9.bank.fx.limits.scope: DSB and Southern Commercial Bank, personal clients
F9.bank.fx.limits.limits: The bank caps date from late 2024, when USD was scarce. Whether they still apply in October 2026, now that rates have stabilised, is unknown. The IMF's February 2026 statement mentions no FX restrictions on individuals. No CBvS or Foreign Exchange Commission page was opened.

F9.cash.border.limit.label: Carrying cash in or out of Suriname
F9.cash.border.limit.value: USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent) may not be carried across Suriname's borders. Suriname's immigration/customs unit (ICF) cites Foreign Exchange Commission Decision No. 225, and says violators are prosecuted and handed to the police. The Rio Times adds that declaring the cash does not make it legal and the cash can be seized.
F9.cash.border.limit.notes: Treat USD 10,000 as a hard ceiling. Arrive with far less.
F9.cash.border.limit.limits: Other sources describe a declaration duty at USD 10,000 rather than a ban, and a 2022 ministerial statement mentions a licence above USD 50,000 for exports (see conflicts). The ICF page is undated. Philippine rules on leaving with cash (BSP limits) are a separate question and were not researched here.

conflicts.value: Prohibited to carry USD 10,000 or more across the border
Exports above USD 10,000 used to need only a declaration; a licence is now needed above 50,000

G.personal.gym.label: Gym membership, monthly
G.personal.gym.notes: A basic gym is about SRD 500 a month (roughly USD 13).
G.personal.gym.limits: Thin Numbeo sample. No gym's own price list found. Older expat posts (2010-2022, not opened) suggested full-service clubs cost much more. Filed under G1 because DATAPOINTS has no personal-care ID.

G.personal.haircut.label: Women's haircut
G.personal.haircut.notes: Salons that take online bookings charge roughly USD 10-40 for a cut. Local salons are likely cheaper.
G.personal.haircut.scope: Paramaribo salons on Fresha: basic cut USD 10, advanced cut 22.50, premium 40; men's clipper cut 15
G.personal.haircut.limits: Online-booking salons only, which skew upmarket. H1.carriers.label: Mobile carriers in Suriname
H1.carriers.value: Two mobile networks: Telesur (state-owned) and Digicel. Both sell prepaid SIMs and eSIMs and have shops in Paramaribo.
H1.carriers.notes: Two choices: Telesur or Digicel. Either works in Paramaribo.
H1.carriers.limits: No coverage map was compared. Coverage in her own street and office is not checked.

H1.esim.label: eSIM availability from local carriers
H1.esim.value: Yes. Telesur sells a prepaid eSIM for SRD 115, the same price as a physical SIM, and can convert a physical SIM to an eSIM at any branch. Digicel sells a 30-day tourist eSIM plan (5 GB, SRD 400, tax excluded).
H1.esim.notes: If her phone takes an eSIM, she can keep her Philippine SIM in the slot and add a Suriname number as an eSIM. That suits the GCash OTP plan (H5).
H1.esim.limits: Neither page says whether an eSIM can be bought online from abroad before arrival or only in a shop. Her phone must support eSIM: dial *#06# and look for an EID.

H1.sim.airport.limits: Digicel's airport hours are tied to Amsterdam arrivals. If she lands on another route (Panama, Miami, Port of Spain, Belém), the kiosk may be closed. GigaGo (2024) says Telesur also sold SIMs at the airport, but Telesur's own pages don't confirm it.

H4.power-cuts.label: Power cuts (EBS load shedding) affecting home internet
H4.power-cuts.value: Since about 25 Aug 2026, EBS has cut power in rotation for at least 3 hours at a time in Paramaribo, Wanica, Para, Commewijne and Saramacca. It can't say in advance which areas. Still going on 14 Oct 2026 (it is also hitting the water supply in Paramaribo-Noord). No end date given.
H4.power-cuts.notes: When the power goes, so does the fibre router. Keep a charged phone with a mobile data bundle and a power bank as the backup. Whether mobile towers stay up during load shedding wasn't checked. Ask landlords whether the building has a generator.
H4.power-cuts.limits: There's no published rotation schedule, and the reports give no figures for how often a given street goes dark. Whether it is still going in late November is unknown.

H4.speeds.label: Typical real-world internet speeds, Suriname (median)
H4.speeds.value: Median fixed download 19.74 Mbps; median mobile download 50.74 Mbps (Ookla data, end 2025). Fixed speeds rose 63% in the year to Aug 2025.
H4.speeds.notes: Either fibre or mobile data is fast enough for a WhatsApp or Zoom video call. A video call needs only a few Mbps. Power cuts, not speed, are what will drop her calls.
H4.speeds.limits: Nationwide medians include old copper and rural lines. A new fibre line in Paramaribo should do much better. No Paramaribo-only figure was found.

H5.gcash-overseas.label: Can GCash be moved to a Suriname number?
H5.gcash-overseas.value: Not as of the lists found. GCash Overseas (sign-up with a foreign mobile number) covered 14-16 named markets (US, Canada, UK, Spain, Italy, Germany, Qatar, Kuwait, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia, plus UAE and Saudi Arabia in other reports). Suriname is not on it. Her GCash stays tied to her Philippine number, which must stay active and able to receive SMS OTPs.
H5.gcash-overseas.notes: Plan on keeping her Philippine SIM alive. Put it in the second slot, or keep it in the phone with a Suriname eSIM, so bank and GCash OTP texts still arrive. Whether Globe or Smart texts reach her in Suriname depends on a roaming partner there, which isn't confirmed (see gaps).
H5.gcash-overseas.limits: The list is from March 2024 and may have grown. Check the GCash app or help centre for the current list.

H6.messaging.value: WhatsApp is used for everyday services, including booking taxis by phone or WhatsApp. Facebook reached about 362,000 people in late 2025, about 80% of adults.

I1.bus.how.label: How Paramaribo's minibuses work
I1.bus.how.value: Privately owned, licensed minibuses run routes from hubs near the Central Market and Heiligenweg (the main terminal sits between Heiligenweg and Knuffelsgracht). There's no timetable, and a bus often leaves when it is full. Wave one down, tell the driver where to stop, and pay cash on board. There's no travel card. Stops are often unmarked.
I1.bus.how.notes: Cheap and used by locals, but there's no timetable and no map, and Canada advises visitors against them. Ask colleagues which line passes her street, and use them by day.
I1.bus.how.limits: No route list or line map was found. Canada's travel advice says 'avoid using public minibuses'. Voja advises against public transport after dark.

I1.ride-apps.label: Ride-hailing apps
I1.ride-apps.value: No Uber, Bolt or Grab. Ride (Ride Technologies N.V., app 'Ride Su') connects passengers with private and licensed taxi drivers in Greater Paramaribo and shows an estimated fare first. Its site doesn't prove it is active today. Most people phone or WhatsApp a taxi company.

I1.taxi.city.label: Taxi ride within Paramaribo
I1.taxi.city.notes: Agree the fare before getting in (Canada). Use licensed taxis or hotel ranks and don't hail from the roadside (UK). Ask a colleague what a normal fare is for her route.
I1.taxi.city.limits: Two travel blogs, and they disagree. Voja's bus fares are clearly out of date, so its taxi range probably is too. With the city bus at SRD 14.50, a taxi at SRD 10 is implausible.

I2.driving-side.label: Which side of the road
I2.driving-side.value: Left. Suriname drives on the left, unlike the Philippines.
I2.driving-side.notes: Traffic keeps left, the opposite of home. Look right first when crossing.

I2.foreign-licence.label: Driving on a Philippine licence: the 'rijtoestemmingsbewijs'
I2.foreign-licence.value: A foreign licence can't be swapped for a Surinamese one. A resident staying more than 2 weeks without a valid international driving permit applies to the KPS Afdeling Rijbewijzen (Nieuwe Haven police station) for a rijtoestemmingsbewijs (driving permission). She needs: the original foreign licence with copies of both sides; a passport copy with the entry stamp; and the original passport. A translation is needed only if the licence isn't in Dutch or English, and a Philippine licence is in English. Fees: SRD 150 state fee and SRD 350 handling. Valid for the length of her legal stay, up to 1 year, and renewable. After 3 years in a row on it she can apply for a Surinamese licence.
I2.foreign-licence.notes: She probably won't drive at first. If she wants to later, getting an IDP in Manila before she leaves is the cheap insurance. After that, a local driving permission costs about SRD 500 in fees (2022 rates).
I2.foreign-licence.limits: The rules and fees date from 2022; confirm with KPS Afdeling Rijbewijzen. Canada's 2026 advice says visitors 'must carry an international driving permit'. How long an IDP alone covers a resident wasn't found. This is not legal advice.

I4.walking-safety.label: Walking, sidewalks and safety at night
I4.walking-safety.value: In Paramaribo most roads are paved but poorly maintained, and many have no sidewalks. Pickpocketing and purse snatching are common in the business and shopping districts and near popular hotels. Armed robbery and carjacking occur. Canada advises avoiding walking alone at night. Both Canada and the UK single out the Palm Garden (Palmentuin). Canada also notes regular demonstrations, especially on Saturdays in Paramaribo, which can disrupt traffic. Canada's risk level is 'take normal security precautions'.
I4.walking-safety.notes: Walk by day and take a known taxi after dark. Phone away and bag across the body in the centre. Avoid the Palmentuin.
I4.walking-safety.limits: Written for visitors, not residents. Nothing specific was found for women living alone (that's J5). The US advisory page couldn't be opened.

J1.doctors.english.label: English-speaking doctors
J1.doctors.english.value: The UK government's list marks every listed provider as English-speaking, including the GPs Drs. E. Berggraaf (Zinniastraat 39, +597 432 565), Drs. G. Stolting (at AZP, +597 442 222) and Drs. I. Tseng (Koningstraat 147, +597 403 578). Expat sources say English is widely used in medicine in Paramaribo, but Dutch is the working language.
J1.doctors.english.notes: Most doctors in Paramaribo can switch to English, so ask: 'Spreekt u Engels?' Phone a GP to confirm before you need them, and ask colleagues who they see.
J1.doctors.english.limits: The only named list is from March 2021, and the expat guide repeats the same three names. Doctors may have moved or retired. The UK does not endorse them.

J1.emergency.where.label: Where to go for urgent but not life-threatening care
J1.emergency.where.value: AZP's emergency department (SEH) asked people in April 2025 to come only for real emergencies (heart attack, stroke, serious accidents), because of renovations and lab problems. For less serious problems it pointed to the GP emergency post (huisartsenspoedpost) at Sint Vincentius and the emergency post at the Zorghotel. Times of Suriname reports a 24/7 GP emergency post at the SZF main office (Fred Derbystraat), a second post on Nieuwweergevondenweg, and a 24/7 pharmacy (Ligeon, Latourweg).
J1.emergency.where.notes: Ask HR in week one which clinic and which GP the company uses, and whether the insurance card works there. Keep the after-hours GP post's address in your phone for a fever at night.
J1.emergency.where.limits: The AZP notice is from April 2025 and may have eased. The Times of Suriname article has no date (© 2026 footer only) and gives no hours or fees for the second post. Canada says there is 'one public emergency room with ambulance services' in Paramaribo.

J1.hospitals.main.value: Academisch Ziekenhuis Paramaribo (AZP, the largest and the national referral hospital, Flustraat, +597 442 222); 's Lands Hospitaal (Tourtonnelaan 3, +597 471 403); Diakonessenhuis (Zinniastraat 64, +597 427 288); Sint Vincentius Ziekenhuis (Catholic, Koninginnestraat 4, +597 471 212); Military Hospital (opposite AZP, +597 440 114).

The Belgian page (Sep 2026) confirms AZP, Sint Vincentius and Diakonessen as the three big hospitals, but gives no phone numbers. The UK list writes 's Lands Hospitaal's street as 'Tourtonnaraan 3'; the street is Tourtonnelaan, so check the address before relying on it.

J1.medicine.shortages.label: Medicine shortages
J1.medicine.shortages.value: Expat guides report shortages, including of medicine for chronic conditions, and advise bringing several months' supply.
J1.medicine.shortages.notes: If she takes anything regularly, bring 3 months' worth and write down the generic (not brand) name, so a Surinamese pharmacist can find the equivalent.
J1.medicine.shortages.limits: Undated expat guide. Search results also pointed to news reports of hospital and pharmacy shortages, but none opened was dated 2026. See gaps.

J1.payment.upfront.label: Paying for care: upfront and deposits
J1.payment.upfront.value: Expect to pay on the spot. The US Commercial Guide (2022) says providers expect immediate payment, and the main hospital with emergency and intensive care asks for a deposit in US dollars or proof of insurance. The UK says some facilities don't bill insurers directly, so you pay and claim it back.
J1.payment.upfront.notes: Keep some US dollars at home for a medical emergency, plus your insurance card and the insurer's assistance number. Ask HR whether the company insurance pays the hospital directly.
J1.payment.upfront.limits: No deposit amount is published. The deposit detail is from 2022.

J2.bring.own.medicine.label: Bringing her own medicine
J2.bring.own.medicine.value: No official Surinamese rule was found. The UK says medicine laws in Suriname may differ, so check before travel. The Belgian government says a proper travel medical kit is required. The expat guide advises several months' supply, prescriptions, a medical summary and generic names, and checking controlled substances.
J2.bring.own.medicine.notes: Pack medicine in its original boxes in hand luggage, with a doctor's letter in English giving the generic name, the dose and 'for personal use'. Ask about anything with codeine, sleeping pills or strong painkillers before you fly.
J2.bring.own.medicine.limits: There is no official quantity limit or list of controlled medicines. Search snippets mention 30-day and 3-month limits, but those sources weren't opened and they disagree. Confirm with the Embassy of Suriname or the employer before flying.

J2.pharmacies.label: Pharmacies (apotheken)
J2.pharmacies.value: Pharmacies (apotheek) are in every part of Paramaribo. A 24/7 pharmacy, Ligeon, is on Latourweg (Times of Suriname).
J2.pharmacies.notes: Find the pharmacy nearest home and work in week one, and ask it how the after-hours duty rota works ('Welke apotheek heeft vanavond dienst?' means 'Which pharmacy is on duty tonight?').
J2.pharmacies.limits: One named 24/7 pharmacy. No source opened gave normal opening hours, the duty-pharmacy (wachtapotheek) rota, or which chains to use. See gaps.

J3.chikungunya.label: Chikungunya (2026 outbreak)
J3.chikungunya.value: Suriname declared a locally spread chikungunya outbreak in January 2026; 134 lab-confirmed cases and one death had been reported by 30 January, including in Paramaribo. The Dutch advice dated 16 Oct 2026 still calls it a current outbreak. Canada says a chikungunya vaccine is approved in Canada; CDC says vaccination is generally not recommended but may be considered.
J3.chikungunya.notes: Chikungunya is the one to watch right now. It is spread by the same day-biting mosquito as dengue. Ask a travel clinic in the Philippines whether the chikungunya vaccine is available and right for her.
J3.chikungunya.limits: There are no case counts after January 2026 from a source we opened; search snippets reported 1,357 positive tests and 8 of 10 districts affected by early March. Whether the vaccine is available in the Philippines is unknown.

J3.dengue.label: Dengue
J3.dengue.value: Dengue is present. Its mosquitoes bite mainly in the daytime. Canada notes there's no vaccine or preventive medicine available there; prevention is avoiding bites. A US guide (2022) says dengue, Zika and chikungunya occur in Paramaribo, especially in the rainy season.
J3.dengue.notes: Same mosquito and same habits as dengue at home in the Philippines: repellent in the daytime too, and empty standing water around the house. If you get a high fever, see a doctor and avoid ibuprofen until dengue is ruled out (ask the doctor).
J3.dengue.limits: There are no current 2026 case counts. The one dengue spike found (Paramaribo Noord and Kwatta) is from January 2023 (Keynews).

J3.prevention.label: Mosquito bite prevention
J3.prevention.value: Suriname's health officials advise removing standing water, covering cisterns and tanks, using repellent, wearing long sleeves and long trousers, and sleeping under nets. CDC adds: avoid swimming in fresh, unchlorinated water (schistosomiasis, leptospirosis).
J3.prevention.notes: Pack one bottle of DEET or picaridin repellent for week one, then buy locally. Window screens and a fan or aircon at night make a real difference.

sources.publisher: Jamaica Observer (quoting Suriname Health Ministry and BOG)

J3.prevention.limits: There's no data on which repellent brands are sold locally or what they cost.

J3.yellowfever.boq.label: Getting the yellow fever shot and yellow card in the Philippines
J3.yellowfever.boq.value: The Bureau of Quarantine (BOQ) gives the vaccine and the International Certificate of Vaccination (yellow card); booking is at icv.boq.ph. Reported stations include Manila (Port Area), SM Mall of Asia, SM North EDSA, Robinsons Manila, Cebu, Iloilo, Davao, Cagayan de Oro and General Santos. The certificate becomes valid 10 days after the shot and is valid for life (WHO rule since 11 July 2016). The fee was reported at about PHP 2,030.
J3.yellowfever.boq.notes: Book now: she needs the shot by about 10 Nov 2026 for a 20 Nov flight. Cebu has a station.
J3.yellowfever.boq.limits: This is from a blog; the BOQ site wasn't opened. The station list and fee need checking at icv.boq.ph. Another search snippet gave PHP 1,500/2,000 for multi-dose/single-dose vials.

J3.yellowfever.certificate.label: Yellow fever certificate at entry
J3.yellowfever.certificate.value: Most official sources say the certificate is required only from travellers aged 1+ arriving from, or transiting more than 12 hours through, a country with yellow fever risk (the Philippines is not one). The Netherlands says proof is mandatory for everyone travelling to Suriname and that people without it may be refused entry. CDC and Canada recommend the vaccine for all travellers anyway.
J3.yellowfever.certificate.notes: Simplest path: get the shot and the yellow card in the Philippines at least 10 days before flying, and carry the card with her passport. It's recommended anyway, and it removes all doubt at the border.
J3.yellowfever.certificate.limits: This depends on her route: a stop in Brazil or another yellow fever country would trigger the rule. The permit side (C6/C7) may add its own health requirements. Confirm with the airline and the Embassy of Suriname.

J4.tapwater.label: Is tap water drinkable in Paramaribo?
J4.tapwater.value: Sources disagree. Belgium (Sep 2026) says tap water is drinkable in Paramaribo only. The water company SWM said in 2023 that its water is safe and meets national and international standards. The Dutch motoring club ANWB says don't drink tap water in Suriname, though Paramaribo's may be drinkable. The Nomads site says not drinkable.
J4.tapwater.notes: Drink bottled or filtered water for the first weeks, then ask the landlord and neighbours what they do. Water from a rooftop tank is a different story from the mains.
J4.tapwater.limits: There's no independent recent test. Water quality at the tap depends on the building's tank and pipes, not just the mains.
