J5.actions.daily.label: Everyday precautions, written as actions
J5.actions.daily.value: 1) Leave gold chains and expensive jewellery at home; keep the phone in a bag, not in your hand at the roadside. 2) Carry a copy of your passport and leave the original locked at home (Belgium). 3) Don't walk alone after dark away from busy, lit areas; go out with others in the evening. 4) Lock car doors and keep windows up while driving. 5) Watch for tricks: people who ask for help at traffic lights, or bags thrown on the windscreen to make you stop (police warning, 2022). 6) Change money only at banks, hotels or official cambios; street exchange is illegal. 7) Steer clear of demonstrations, which happen often on Saturdays in Paramaribo. 8) Never carry a package for someone else: all drugs are illegal and penalties are harsh.
J5.actions.daily.notes: Very like big-city habits in Cebu or Manila. The difference is that robbers here sometimes carry weapons, so if it happens, hand it over and don't resist.
J5.actions.daily.limits: The traffic-light and windscreen tricks come from a July 2022 police warning.

J5.areas.label: Places to take extra care
J5.areas.value: UK: quiet or secluded parts of Paramaribo, including the Palm Garden (Palmentuin), plus the busy business and shopping districts for pickpockets. The Netherlands: streets and parks outside the nightlife area. Belgium: the hotel district is relatively safe, and non-tourist neighbourhoods see more attacks. Outside the city, Canada names Albina, Moengo, the East–West and Afobakka highways and Brokopondo district for robbery.
J5.areas.notes: See the Palmentuin and the waterfront by day, with company. Ask colleagues which streets they avoid near home.
J5.areas.limits: There's no neighbourhood-level list for where to live; that's E1 in another group.

J5.crime.pattern.label: What crime looks like
J5.crime.pattern.value: Mostly opportunistic: pickpocketing and bag snatching in the shopping and business areas and near hotels, plus burglary, armed robbery and home invasions. Foreigners are often targeted. Criminals may carry firearms or machetes (kapmessen). Police figures for 3–30 Aug 2026, country-wide: 15 armed robberies, 33 robberies without a firearm, 124 burglaries and 3 homicides. Belgium says crime has fallen in recent years but remains at an average level.
J5.crime.pattern.notes: This is mostly crime of opportunity. The aim is to give nobody the opportunity. The actions below do most of the work.
J5.crime.pattern.limits: The police figures are national and cover one month. There's no breakdown by neighbourhood.

J5.taxis.night.label: Getting home at night
J5.taxis.night.value: UK: use only licensed taxis or those on official hotel ranks, and don't hail taxis from the roadside. Belgium: limit evening and night travel and preferably travel with others. Canada: avoid walking alone after dark away from major hotels.
J5.taxis.night.notes: Get one or two taxi numbers from HR or colleagues in week one, and phone for a car instead of flagging one down. Share your trip with a friend on WhatsApp after dark.
J5.taxis.night.limits: Which taxi companies or ride apps are trusted is I1, in another group.

J5.woman.alone.label: Living alone as a woman
J5.woman.alone.value: None of the government advisories (Canada, UK, Netherlands, Belgium) carries women-specific advice for Suriname. On Nomads.com, contributors rate 'Safe for women' as 'Bad' and overall safety as 'Okay'. Burglary is the most common serious crime (124 reported nationally in four weeks of Aug 2026), and the US flags home invasions.
J5.woman.alone.notes: Choose a flat with burglar bars, a gate and a lock you trust, ideally in a compound or with neighbours close by. Don't say you live alone to strangers or drivers. Keep one trusted contact who knows where you are in the evenings. Join a church or work group in month one so you have people to call.
J5.woman.alone.limits: The Nomads rating rests on 17 reviews, mostly short-stay visitors. No first-hand account from a woman expat living alone was found. See gaps.

J6.consular.help.label: Philippine consular help in an emergency
J6.consular.help.value: There's no Philippine embassy in Suriname. The Philippine Embassy in Brasília covers it (+55 61 3224-8694; +55 61 9 9389-3042), and an honorary consul in Paramaribo, Mr. Egon Lyndon Audhoe (Laparkan Suriname NV), works by appointment.
J6.consular.help.notes: Before flying, write down the Brasília embassy's number and the honorary consul's, and register with the embassy if it offers registration.
J6.consular.help.limits: Both are third-party directories. The DFA's own page (dfa.gov.ph/suriname) blocked our reader. A search snippet of it gave a different address (Nieuwe Charlesburgweg 95) and phone (+597 8798669). Confirm with DFA. This overlaps B6.

J6.emergency.numbers.label: Emergency numbers

J6.emergency.numbers.notes: Save these on day one: 115 (police), 113 (ambulance), 110 (fire). Also save her own hospital's number and a taxi. 112 (the EU number) is not on any official Surinamese list.
J6.emergency.numbers.limits: 115 for police and 110 for fire are consistent across sources. The ambulance number varies, and the helpline numbers conflict (see conflicts).

J7.advisory.belgium.value: Crime in Paramaribo and around Albina has fallen in recent years but remains at an average level; the hotel district is relatively safe. Last updated 8 Sep 2026.

J7.advisory.canada.limits: This is written for Canadian travellers.

J7.advisory.netherlands.label: Netherlands travel advice for Suriname
J7.advisory.netherlands.value: Colour code yellow ('geel': travel possible, with particular security risks). Last changed 16 Oct 2026, still valid on 20 Oct 2026.
J7.advisory.netherlands.notes: The Dutch advice is the most detailed, since many Dutch people travel there. It flags the chikungunya outbreak and the yellow fever card.

J7.advisory.uk.label: UK travel advice for Suriname

J7.advisory.uk.notes: The UK advice is calm. Its main practical points are licensed taxis only, and Palmentuin and quiet areas with care.

K1.languages.label: Languages: Dutch, Sranan Tongo, English
K1.languages.value: Dutch is the official language (government, schools, contracts) and is spoken natively by about 60% of people. Sranan Tongo is the everyday lingua franca: markets, taxis, small shops, neighbourhood talk. Hindustani (Sarnami), Javanese and others are also spoken. English: 'almost all business contacts in the capital speak English' (US Commercial Guide, 2022), and Nomads rates English-speaking 'Good'. An expat guide (Apr 2026) says you can get by with mainly English in professional circles, but Dutch is essential with institutions.
K1.languages.notes: English will get her through work meetings and most shops in Paramaribo. Dutch opens government offices and paperwork. A few Sranan words win smiles at the market. Whether her own office works in Dutch is A7: ask the employer.
K1.languages.limits: The '60% native Dutch' figure comes from older census data; no 2024 census language figures were found. The Wikipedia figure for Sranan is 520,000 first-language speakers (2018).

K2.phrase.01.label: Hello / good morning
K2.phrase.01.value: Dutch: Hallo (HAH-low); Goedemorgen (GOO-duh-MORE-gun); Goedemiddag (GOO-duh-MIH-dahgh, afternoon). Sranan: Odi (OH-dee), or 'Odi masra' to a man, 'Odi misi' to a woman.
K2.phrase.01.limits: The Sranan list is from 1995 and gives no pronunciation; the Sranan hints are our approximation (vowels sound much like Cebuano vowels).

K2.phrase.02.label: How are you? / I'm fine
K2.phrase.02.value: Dutch: Hoe gaat het? (hoo GAHT hut). Sranan: Fa waka? (fah WAH-kah) or Fa yu tan? (fah yoo TAHN). Reply: Mi bun (mee BOON) = I'm fine.
K2.phrase.02.limits: The Sranan pronunciation hint is our approximation.

K2.phrase.03.label: Thank you
K2.phrase.03.value: Dutch: Dank u (DAHNK uu, polite) / Dank je (DAHNK yuh, friends). Sranan: Grantangi (grahn-TAHN-gee).
K2.phrase.03.notes: Use 'Dank u' with older people and at the office.
K2.phrase.03.limits: The Sranan pronunciation hint is our approximation.

K2.phrase.04.label: Please
K2.phrase.04.notes: In Dutch 'alstublieft' also means 'here you are' when handing something over.
K2.phrase.04.limits: No Sranan word for 'please' was found in a source we opened.

K2.phrase.05.label: Excuse me / sorry
K2.phrase.05.value: Dutch: Pardon (PAR-don) to get attention or pass by; Sorry (SOH-ree); Het spijt me (het SPAYT muh) = I'm sorry.

K2.phrase.06.label: Yes / no
K2.phrase.06.value: Dutch: Ja (YAH) / Nee (NAY). Sranan: Ay (EYE) = yes.
K2.phrase.06.limits: The Sranan word for 'no' wasn't in the list we opened.

K2.phrase.07.label: Do you speak English?
K2.phrase.07.value: Dutch: Spreekt u Engels? (SPRAYKT uu ENG-uls)
K2.phrase.07.notes: The most useful sentence of week one. The answer is usually yes.

K2.phrase.08.label: I don't understand / I don't speak Dutch
K2.phrase.08.value: Dutch: Ik begrijp het niet (ick buh-GRAYP hut neet); Ik spreek geen Nederlands (ick SPRAYK gayn NAY-dur-lahnts).

K2.phrase.09.label: How much is this?
K2.phrase.09.value: Dutch: Hoeveel kost dit? (HOO-vale kost dit). Sranan: Omeni? (OH-meh-nee).
K2.phrase.09.notes: 'Omeni?' at the market, 'Hoeveel kost dit?' in a shop.
K2.phrase.09.limits: The Sranan pronunciation hint is our approximation.

K2.phrase.10.label: Where is the toilet? / Do you know where I can find ...?
K2.phrase.10.value: Dutch: Waar is het toilet? (wahr is hut twah-LET). Sranan: Yu sabi pe mi man feni ...? (yoo SAH-bee peh mee mahn FEH-nee) = Do you know where I can find ...?
K2.phrase.10.limits: The Sranan pronunciation hint is our approximation.

K3.filipino.community.label: Filipino community in Suriname
K3.filipino.community.value: There is a small community; no size figure came from a source we could open. Philippine government news (2014–2022, seen only as search snippets) describes a few hundred to about 1,000 Filipino workers, many of them nurses (once about 70 at AZP), plus engineers and workers in fishing, mining and hospitality. Consular help comes from the Philippine Embassy in Brasília, with an honorary consul in Paramaribo (see J6.consular.help). No named association or Facebook group was found.
K3.filipino.community.notes: The way in is through people: ask the honorary consul, the nurses at AZP, and the Catholic parish. Search Facebook for 'Filipinos in Suriname' and 'Pinoy Suriname' once she's there.
K3.filipino.community.limits: The DFA news pages that give community size (2014, 2015, 2018, 2022) blocked our reader and are seen only as search snippets. The figures conflict: about 1,000 in 2014, about 800 in 2015 and about 500 in 2018. See gaps.

K4.catholic.cathedral.label: Saints Peter and Paul Cathedral Basilica (Kathedrale Basiliek Sint Petrus en Paulus)
K4.catholic.cathedral.value: Gravenstraat 14, central Paramaribo; +597 472 521. A Mass listing shows Saturday vigil 7:00 pm and Sunday 10:00 am. Suriname has one Catholic diocese, the Diocese of Paramaribo. The basilica is open to visitors, with a shop at the back selling candles and rosaries.
K4.catholic.cathedral.notes: Phone the cathedral or check its Facebook in week one to confirm times. The big wooden basilica is worth seeing on the first Sunday even before she knows the schedule. For Christmas Masses, ask early in December.
K4.catholic.cathedral.limits: Mass times come from an undated volunteer listing (a search summary also showed 7:15 pm). The diocese site has no Mass schedule page. The language of Mass wasn't stated; Dutch is likely but unconfirmed.

K4.catholic.parishes.label: Other Catholic churches in Paramaribo
K4.catholic.parishes.value: Within about 4 km of the cathedral: Heilig Hart Kerk, St. Rosa Kerk, St. Alfonsus Kerk, St. Bonifacius Kerk, Onze Lieve Vrouw van Fatima Kerk, Onze Lieve Vrouw van Nazareth Kerk, Heilige Familie Kerk, Zacheus Kerk, St. Augustinus Kerk, St. Jozef Kerk.
K4.catholic.parishes.notes: Once she knows where she'll live, pick the nearest parish. The Diocese's Facebook page (facebook.com/bisdomparamaribo) and Radio Immanuel are where parish news appears.
K4.catholic.parishes.limits: This is a list of churches only, with no Mass times or languages. No English-language Catholic Mass was confirmed; a 2022 diplomat's report says English-language religious services exist in Paramaribo without naming them.

K5.nov.dec.weather.label: November–March weather in Paramaribo
K5.nov.dec.weather.value: Average high/low and rain (1991–2020): Nov 31.2/24.8 °C, 126 mm, 13 rain days; Dec 30.0/24.2 °C, 184 mm, 18 rain days; Jan 29.2/24.1 °C, 173 mm; Feb 29.4/23.2 °C, 146 mm; Mar 28.7/23.5 °C, 131 mm. Humidity is about 73–78%.
K5.nov.dec.weather.notes: It's like Cebu in the rainy months: about 30 °C every day, with short, heavy afternoon showers.

K5.packing.label: What to pack for the climate
K5.packing.value: Pack for humidity and rain even in the 'dry' months (Responsible Travel). That means light, breathable office clothes, a compact umbrella, sandals that can get wet, long sleeves and long trousers for mosquito evenings, sunscreen and repellent. A cardigan helps for air-conditioned offices and churches.
K5.packing.notes: She already owns the right wardrobe from the Philippines. Add an umbrella that lives in her bag.
K5.packing.limits: Only 'pack for humidity and rain' and 'bring bug spray and sun lotion' come from sources; the item list is our practical reading of them.

K5.seasons.label: Wet and dry seasons
K5.seasons.value: Roughly: long dry season mid-August to late November or early December; short rains early December to early February; short dry season February–April; long rainy season late April to mid-August (May–June wettest). Paramaribo has no truly dry month: every month averages over 60 mm of rain.
K5.seasons.notes: She lands at the turn from the dry season into the short rains: hot, with more and more afternoon downpours through December.
K5.seasons.limits: Season boundaries vary by year and by source. Canada also says El Niño is expected to strengthen into 2027, which may bring drought, floods or storms.

K6.work.culture.label: Office work culture
K6.work.culture.value: Business hours are usually 8:00 am–4:30 pm Monday–Friday, with some offices open 8:00 am–1:00 pm on Saturday. Government offices open about 7:00 am–2:30 pm and close early on Fridays and before holidays. On dress, suits are worn, but the heat makes smart-casual acceptable in most meetings (not with senior officials); a diplomat's report calls it 'business casual'. Relationships come first: people build trust before getting down to business, and decisions take time. Business cards are exchanged. The pace is more relaxed than in the US.
K6.work.culture.notes: Expect office life to feel familiar from the Philippines: early starts, relationship first, and meetings that may start a little late. Dress smart-casual in week one and copy her colleagues. Be on time herself even if others aren't.
K6.work.culture.limits: The sources are from 2022 and written from a US business-visitor angle. Her own office's hours and dress code are A7: ask the employer.

K8.timezone.label: Time zone vs Manila and Toronto
K8.timezone.value: Suriname is UTC−3 all year (no daylight saving). Manila is UTC+8, so Manila is 11 hours ahead: 8 pm in Paramaribo is 7 am the next day in Manila. Toronto is UTC−5 in winter, so Paramaribo is 2 hours ahead of Toronto from 1 Nov 2026 to 14 Mar 2027, and 1 hour ahead the rest of the year.
K8.timezone.notes: Best time to call home: her evening (7–10 pm) is Manila's morning (6–9 am). A call at 7 am Paramaribo time reaches Manila at 6 pm.
K8.timezone.limits: The DST dates are worked out from the Canada rule (first Sunday of November, second Sunday of March).

K9.plugs.voltage.label: Plug type and voltage
K9.plugs.voltage.value: It's 60 Hz like the Philippines, but the voltage is usually lower: mostly 127 V, sometimes 220 V. Sockets can be US-style (A/B) or European round-pin (C/F). Phone and laptop chargers marked 100–240 V work with only a plug adapter. Hairdryers, rice cookers and other 220 V-only appliances may not work on a 127 V socket.
K9.plugs.voltage.notes: Bring a universal travel adapter. Check the label on each appliance: if it says 100–240 V, it's fine. Leave the Philippine 220 V-only hairdryer or rice cooker at home and buy local.
K9.plugs.voltage.limits: There's no statement from the utility (EBS). Buildings vary, and some have both 127 V and 220 V outlets.

K9.shopping.label: Where to shop for clothes and electronics
K9.shopping.value: The main malls for electronics, clothes and household goods are Hermitage Mall (described as the largest) and Maretraite Plaza/Mall. The Centrale Markt sells produce and household items. Imported goods are expensive: an expat site cites 25–40% duties on electronics and branded clothes. Many expats order from the US through Miami-based forwarders (SkyBox and EZ Ship are named).
K9.shopping.notes: Bring the laptop, phone and any electronics she needs from the Philippines, since they cost more in Suriname. Clothes and basics are fine to buy locally.
K9.shopping.limits: This rests on one undated secondary source, and there are no prices for specific items. Mall opening hours were not found.

P1.dmw.directhire.label: DMW processing for a direct hire (no Philippine agency)
P1.dmw.directhire.value: Philippine rules bar direct hiring of OFWs unless the hire is exempt (e.g. professionals and skilled workers on terms above the DMW standard, up to five per employer) or processed through a licensed agency. Exempt direct hires still register with DMW before leaving.
P1.dmw.directhire.notes: Ask the employer: are you hiring me through a DMW-licensed agency, or as an exempt direct hire? Who files the DMW paperwork, and when?

sources.publisher: Migrant Workers Office checklist (via Philippine Consulate Vancouver)

P1.dmw.directhire.limits: The DMW site renders with JavaScript and its detail pages could not be read; the rule comes from the MWO checklist (citing DMW Dept. Circular 01 s.2023) and older POEA guidance. No 2026 change found, but none ruled out.

P2.dmw.oec.label: OEC / OFW Pass (exit clearance)
P2.dmw.oec.value: Every departing OFW needs an exit clearance. DMW is replacing the paper OEC with a digital OFW Pass (DMW Mobile App / eGovPH), but reports say the Pass covers returning workers (Balik-Manggagawa) first, and first-time hires may still go through the conventional OEC. The OEC exemption is for returning workers, not a first deployment.
P2.dmw.oec.notes: Ask the employer or agency: will I get an OEC or an OFW Pass, and will it be in hand before my flight date?
P2.dmw.oec.limits: Rollout status conflicts across 2025-2026 news; no DMW advisory could be read directly. One third-party guide cites a direct-hire OEC fee near USD 100 (unverified, not used).

conflicts.value: OFW Pass fully replaces the OEC by early 2026
OFW Pass for Balik-Manggagawa only; first-timers still use the OEC
conflicts.source: DMW post as reported in news

P3.dmw.suriname.label: Is Suriname an allowed deployment destination?
P3.dmw.suriname.value: Suriname was on the list of countries certified as compliant under RA 10022 (reported 2012). No deployment ban on Suriname was found, but no current DMW list was found either.
P3.dmw.suriname.notes: Ask DMW (or the agency) to confirm Suriname is cleared for deployment today, with no ban or watch-list issue.
P3.dmw.suriname.limits: The newest list found is from 2012; lists change (192 countries by 2015). Seen through search results only.

P4.pdos.label: PDOS (Pre-Departure Orientation Seminar)
P4.pdos.value: First-time land-based OFWs attend a PDOS (run through OWWA or accredited providers) before the exit clearance is released.
P4.pdos.notes: Ask: when and where is my PDOS, online or in person, and does it have to be done before the OEC is issued?
P4.pdos.limits: owwa.gov.ph returned 403 to our fetch, so the page itself was not read. Stated from general knowledge of the process; confirm format (online or in person) and schedule.

P5.owwa.label: OWWA membership
P5.owwa.value: OWWA membership comes with OFW processing and gives welfare, repatriation and some insurance-type benefits. It is normally paid at processing and valid per contract.
P5.owwa.notes: Ask: is OWWA membership included in my processing, who pays it, and what does it cover while I'm in Suriname?
P5.owwa.limits: Official page blocked to our fetch (403); no fee figure given because none was verified.

P6.sss.philhealth.pagibig.label: Keeping SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG going as an OFW
P6.sss.philhealth.pagibig.value: SSS is compulsory for land-based OFWs under RA 11199 (she pays as if self-employed; upheld by the Supreme Court, G.R. 248680, Nov 2024). PhilHealth: OFWs are direct contributors at 5% of monthly income (PHP 500 floor, PHP 5,000 ceiling per secondary 2026 guides). Pag-IBIG membership is mandatory for OFWs. All three can be paid from abroad.
P6.sss.philhealth.pagibig.notes: She's an accountant, so she'll want the numbers: confirm her SSS bracket and PhilHealth rate with each agency, and set up online payment (My.SSS, PhilHealth member portal, Virtual Pag-IBIG) before leaving.
P6.sss.philhealth.pagibig.limits: The three agency homepages were reachable but rate tables were not read from them. PhilHealth figures are from secondary 2026 guides; a bill to exempt OFWs from direct premiums was reported pending in early 2026.

conflicts.value: PHP 400 monthly minimum

P7.apostille.label: Which documents usually need an apostille
P7.apostille.value: Both the Philippines (since 14 May 2019) and Suriname are parties to the Apostille Convention, so Philippine public documents for Suriname get a DFA apostille, not embassy legalisation. Usually: diploma and transcript (CHED/school certification first), PSA birth certificate, NBI clearance, and professional licence (CPA/PRC) if asked.
P7.apostille.notes: Ask the employer for the exact list of documents the Suriname work permit needs apostilled, then book the DFA appointment early; it is the usual bottleneck.
P7.apostille.limits: HCCH table confirmed both countries are parties. The DFA page returned 403, so appointment and fee details were not read. Which documents Suriname wants is the employer's call.

P8.bi.departure.label: BI departure checks at NAIA (offloading)
P8.bi.departure.value: Immigration officers check that an OFW holds a valid exit clearance (OEC/OFW Pass), the work visa or permit, the contract and an eTravel registration. Revised IACAT departure guidelines (Sept 2023) list documents officers may ask for at secondary inspection. A trip that doesn't fly straight to the job country (e.g. a Toronto stopover) may draw questions.
P8.bi.departure.notes: Carry paper copies of everything: OEC/OFW Pass, contract, Suriname permit/visa, the full ticket through to Paramaribo, and the employer's contact. Ask the employer or agency whether a stopover in Canada needs to show on the OEC.
P8.bi.departure.scope: NAIA and other PH international airports
P8.bi.departure.limits: The BI homepage was read, but no current OFW departure checklist was found on it. The IACAT details are from 2023 news reports, and no 2025-26 revision was confirmed.

P9.yellowfever.label: Yellow fever certificate
P9.yellowfever.value: Suriname requires a yellow fever certificate from travellers arriving within 6 days of leaving or transiting a country with yellow fever risk, issued at least 10 days before arrival. The Philippines and Canada are not risk countries, but Panama, Trinidad and Guyana (common connections) are, and Suriname itself is. Vaccination is recommended for all travellers to Suriname aged 9 months and over.
P9.yellowfever.notes: Simplest path: get the yellow fever shot and the yellow card (ICVP) from the Bureau of Quarantine in the Philippines at least 10 days before landing in Paramaribo, whatever the route.
P9.yellowfever.limits: The airline page is from Jan 2024; the WHO item is from 2017. 2025-26 reports describe yellow fever spreading in South America. The BOQ (Bureau of Quarantine) site did not respond.

X1.food.asian-groceries.fun: No Filipino aisle confirmed yet. The Chinese Market on Ma Retraiteweg is hunt number one.
X1.food.asian-groceries.label: Asian groceries (Filipino ingredients not yet confirmed)
X1.food.asian-groceries.value: Surinam Airways' shopping guide lists the Chinese Market on Ma Retraiteweg (imported Chinese goods, fresh produce, household items) and Choi's Supermarket & Mall (groceries and specialty items). Roopram Roti's specialty shop sells Indian snacks and ingredients. No opened source names a shop stocking Filipino brands.
X1.food.asian-groceries.notes: Week-one mission: walk the Chinese Market aisles and report back.

X1.food.bakabana.fun: Fried ripe plantain with peanut sauce. Turon's long-lost Surinamese cousin, honestly.
X1.food.bakabana.label: Bakabana (fried plantain with peanut sauce)
X1.food.bakabana.value: Ripe plantain fried in batter, served with spicy peanut sauce, sold from street carts, stalls and evening food stands.
X1.food.bakabana.limits: The price is the blog's range for fried plantain snacks generally, not bakabana specifically. No photo found.

X1.food.bami-nasi.fun: Pancit's Javanese-Surinamese cousin, with satay and peanut sauce on the side.
X1.food.bami-nasi.imageCredit: Laig, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X1.food.bami-nasi.label: Bami and nasi (Javanese-Surinamese noodles and fried rice)
X1.food.bami-nasi.value: Bami (fried egg noodles, darker than Indonesian bami) and nasi (fried rice), typically with satay, fried egg, sambal and peanut sauce. Everyday lunch at warungs and Chinese-Surinamese eateries.
X1.food.bami-nasi.limits: The two SRD prices come from the same publisher in the same month and differ about fourfold; treat as a very wide range until she sees real menus.

SRD 90-150 (bami or nasi with satay and peanut sauce)

X1.food.bara.fun: Lentil fritter rings with chutney for breakfast. Ukoy energy, different shape.
X1.food.bara.imageCredit: Sebleouf, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X1.food.bara.label: Bara (and pholourie)
X1.food.bara.value: Hindustani-Surinamese fritter of lentils and yellow split peas, shaped as a small ring, eaten as a snack with tamarind chutney or chilli sauce. Bara, pholourie or a sandwich makes a Central Market breakfast.
X1.food.bara.limits: Price is one blog's breakfast range at the Central Market. Photo is a Surinamese bara served in Rotterdam (2019).

X1.food.javanese-warungs.fun: Blauwgrond after dark: family warungs, big portions, small prices. Taxi there, roll home.
X1.food.javanese-warungs.label: Javanese warungs (Blauwgrond and Lelydorp)
X1.food.javanese-warungs.value: Blauwgrond, about 15 minutes by car from the centre, is packed with family-run Javanese warungs, mostly open in the evening, with large portions at low prices. Named: Mirosso (Blauwgrond, long-running; bami sells out) and Bibit (closer to the centre). Chicken satay is a warung staple. Take a taxi; too far to walk.
X1.food.javanese-warungs.notes: Ask colleagues for their favourite warung; everyone has one.
X1.food.javanese-warungs.limits: Satay price from one 2026 blog. Named warungs from one undated guide; check they are still open. No photo found.

X1.food.moksi-alesi.fun: Rice, salted meat, dried fish and beans in one pot. Peak comfort food.
X1.food.moksi-alesi.label: Moksi alesi
X1.food.moksi-alesi.value: Creole 'mixed rice' cooked in one pot with salted meat, dried fish, beans and vegetables.
X1.food.moksi-alesi.unit: lunch plate (listed together with nasi and bami)
X1.food.moksi-alesi.limits: Only price is a bundled itinerary figure; see the bami/nasi conflict. No freely licensed photo found.

X1.food.pastei.fun: A chicken pot pie with raisins, star of Creole celebrations. Save room.
X1.food.pastei.label: Pastei (Creole chicken pie)
X1.food.pastei.value: Dutch-Creole chicken-and-vegetable pot pie with raisins and citrus, called the Creole celebration centrepiece.
X1.food.pastei.limits: Only one opened source, undated. No price, no named place to buy it, no photo found.

X1.food.pom.fun: Suriname's party dish, and they also put it in a sandwich. Broodje pom, please.
X1.food.pom.imageCredit: Alfredo1980 (assumed; no machine-readable author), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X1.food.pom.label: Pom (and broodje pom)
X1.food.pom.value: Baked dish of grated pomtajer root over chicken with citrus juice, tomato and spices; of Creole/Portuguese-Jewish origin and the best-known Surinamese festive dish. Also sold as broodje pom (pom in a bread roll) at market stalls. Suriname-guide names Soela (Waterkant) for pom with chicken.
X1.food.pom.unit: plate with rice and salad, mid-range eatery
X1.food.pom.limits: Price is one travel blog's 2026 range. Table Journey says pom is often only on menus at weekends or celebrations.

X1.food.roti.fun: Curry, potato and long beans folded into soft roti. Hands only, no spoon needed.
X1.food.roti.imageCredit: Laig, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X1.food.roti.label: Roti with curry
X1.food.roti.value: Hindustani-Surinamese flatbread (dhalpuri or aloo puri) served with curried chicken, potato and kousenband (long beans), often with a boiled egg; also sold as a wrap. Named roti shops: Roopram Roti (near the Waterkant) and Joosje Roti Shop (Zwartenhovenbrugstraat). Shops often sell out early.
X1.food.roti.notes: Suriname's everyday favourite. Go before the lunch rush; the good shops sell out.
X1.food.roti.limits: Price is one travel blog's 2026 range, not observed menus. The photo shows a Surinamese roti, not a specific Paramaribo shop.

X1.food.saoto.fun: Clear chicken soup for breakfast, tinola-adjacent, with sambal and crispy potato sticks.
X1.food.saoto.label: Saoto soup
X1.food.saoto.value: Javanese-Surinamese chicken soup: clear turmeric broth with shredded chicken, bean sprouts, fried potato sticks, egg and sambal, over rice. Mainly a breakfast dish; warungs open from about 7am and often run out before noon. Souposo (Waterkant) is named for saoto and peanut soup; Lelydorp and Blauwgrond warungs are the go-to.
X1.food.saoto.limits: No price on any page opened (a search snippet said SRD 40-70, but that page would not load). No freely licensed photo of Surinamese saoto found.

X2.place.cathedral.fun: Your Sunday parish might be the largest wooden structure in the Western Hemisphere.
X2.place.cathedral.imageCredit: Likazolo52, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X2.place.cathedral.label: Saint Peter and Paul Cathedral Basilica
X2.place.cathedral.value: Wikipedia: 'the largest wooden structure in the Western Hemisphere'. Built from 1883, consecrated 1885, towers finished 1901; restored with EU funding and re-opened on 13 November 2010; made a minor basilica by Pope Francis in 2014. The priest Peter (Peerke) Donders is buried here. Entry is free, with optional donations.
X2.place.cathedral.limits: Donation range from one blog. The size claim is Wikipedia's; the 2014 blog phrases it as a question.

conflicts.value: the largest wooden structure in the Western Hemisphere
one of the largest wooden cathedrals in the region

X2.place.central-market.fun: Food downstairs, everything else upstairs. Go early; it winds down by lunch.
X2.place.central-market.imageCredit: -JvL- from Netherlands, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X2.place.central-market.label: Central Market (Centrale Markt)
X2.place.central-market.value: Two-storey market on the Waterkant by the river, open Monday to Saturday: food downstairs (fruit, vegetables, meat, fish, dried fish, spices, Madame Jeanette peppers, ready-to-eat snacks), general goods upstairs. Busiest early morning; trade runs from early until about 1pm.
X2.place.central-market.limits: Closing time (about 1pm) from one undated guide.

X2.place.fort-zeelandia.fun: A 17th-century fort with a museum of colonial furniture and old photos.
X2.place.fort-zeelandia.imageCredit: Jashda, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X2.place.fort-zeelandia.label: Fort Zeelandia and the Surinaams Museum
X2.place.fort-zeelandia.value: A wooden fort was built here in 1640, reinforced by the English as Fort Willoughby, and taken by the Dutch in 1667. It houses the Surinaams Museum (ethnographica, archaeology, colonial furniture, textiles, historic photos) and the Nola Hatterman Art Academy. It also carries a dark history: the 'December murders' of 1982 took place here.
X2.place.fort-zeelandia.notes: Pair it with a walk along the Waterkant.
X2.place.fort-zeelandia.limits: Entry fee and opening hours not found on any opened page.

X2.place.hermitage-mall.fun: A cinema, smoothie bars and beauty shops under one roof. Closed Sundays, though.
X2.place.hermitage-mall.imageCredit: Ymnes, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X2.place.hermitage-mall.label: Hermitage Mall
X2.place.hermitage-mall.value: Described as the largest mall in Paramaribo (Surinam Airways) or Suriname (Wanderlog): fashion, jewellery, shoes, toys, beauty stores, electronics, Hard Rock Cafe Suriname, McDonald's, Popeyes, smoothie bars, a cinema, a gym and grocery stores. Hours: Mon-Thu 9am-9pm, Fri-Sat 9am-10pm, closed Sunday (some shops close earlier).

sources.publisher: Surinam Airways, Explore Suriname: 'Shopping: Suriname's Retail Treasures'

X2.place.hermitage-mall.limits: Hours and tenants from an undated aggregator listing. Photo from 2022.

X2.place.inner-city.fun: A whole UNESCO old town of white wooden houses. Your daily walk is heritage.
X2.place.inner-city.imageCredit: Ron Van Oers, CC BY-SA 3.0 igo, via Wikimedia Commons
X2.place.inner-city.label: Historic inner city of Paramaribo (UNESCO World Heritage)
X2.place.inner-city.value: On the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2002. After the 1821 fire the Waterkant was rebuilt with monumental white wooden buildings with galleries; the Palmentuin is cited specifically in the listing. A police help post at Wakapasi was announced in April 2026 to tackle theft and vandalism in the historic centre.

sources.publisher: Key News Suriname (tag page; newest item 2 Aug 2026)

X2.place.inner-city.limits: Facts from Wikipedia (UNESCO's own page returned 403). Photo is from 2005.

X2.place.mosque-synagogue.fun: A mosque and a synagogue as next-door neighbours. Paramaribo's personality, one street.
X2.place.mosque-synagogue.imageCredit: Harveypinas, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X2.place.mosque-synagogue.label: Mosque Keizerstraat and Neveh Shalom Synagogue, side by side
X2.place.mosque-synagogue.value: The Ahmadiyya mosque on Keizerstraat (current building 1984; Muhammad Ali visited the earlier one in 1979) stands next to the Neveh Shalom Synagogue (current building completed 1842), which holds a small museum on Jewish history in Suriname. Both are listed as free to enter, dress code permitting.
X2.place.mosque-synagogue.limits: Visiting hours and the synagogue museum's opening times not found.

X2.place.palmentuin.fun: Royal palms and capuchin monkeys. Daytime only, and check it's actually open first.
X2.place.palmentuin.imageCredit: -JvL- from Netherlands, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X2.place.palmentuin.label: Palmentuin (Garden of Palms): check it is open, daytime only
X2.place.palmentuin.value: Royal-palm garden behind the Presidential Palace, opened to the public in 1685, home to tropical birds and a troop of capuchin monkeys; cited in the UNESCO listing. Closed since November 2022 for rehabilitation; in September 2024 the work was reported halted. No opened source confirms it has reopened.
X2.place.palmentuin.notes: Safety caveat: go in daylight, not alone after dark, keep the phone away. Don't feed the monkeys.

sources.publisher: Key News Suriname (tag page; newest item 2 Aug 2026)

X2.place.palmentuin.limits: Current open/closed status unknown as of Oct 2026. Safety: Take Your Backpack (2026) lists the Palmentuin among petty-theft spots; a 2014 blog was warned of drug users there. Photo from 2016.

X2.place.peperpot.fun: Sloths, monkeys and a 12-metre birding tower, five kilometres from the city.
X2.place.peperpot.imageCredit: Dan Lundberg, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X2.place.peperpot.label: Peperpot Nature Park
X2.place.peperpot.value: Former coffee and cocoa plantation in Commewijne, about 5 km from Paramaribo across the river (Hadji Iding Soemitaweg 32). About 81 ha visitor park within 820 ha: flat trails, a 12 m birding tower, monkeys, sloths and many birds. Open daily 8am-5pm. Bikes can be rented nearby.
X2.place.peperpot.notes: Go early; bring water and mosquito repellent. Photo: a three-toed sloth at Peperpot (2019).
X2.place.peperpot.limits: Entry fee unconfirmed: Wanderlog's listing says free admission, but a search snippet quoted a review saying SRD 250 (not opened). Confirm on +597 354-547 / 881-5533 (WhatsApp).

X2.place.waterkant.fun: River views, food stalls and a freshly redone boulevard. Evening stroll, sorted.
X2.place.waterkant.imageCredit: Otter, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X2.place.waterkant.label: Waterkant (riverside promenade)
X2.place.waterkant.value: Paramaribo's oldest street, along the Suriname River from Onafhankelijkheidsplein to the Central Market, lined with food stalls and terraces; the ferry to Meerzorg leaves here. Redeveloped under the Paramaribo Urban Rehabilitation Program: in November 2025 the stretch to the Stenen Trap reopened with a new Craft Market, terraces, a small park, a playground, a boulevard and public toilets. A new amphitheatre on the old flag square is managed by the Ministry of Transport, Communication and Tourism. A public yoga session was held here on 14 March 2026.
X2.place.waterkant.notes: Part of the UNESCO area. Take the usual petty-theft care (see the safety section).
X2.place.waterkant.limits: The amphitheatre article gives 5 December as the opening day but no year. Photo is from 2016, before the redevelopment.

X3.trip.bigi-pan.fun: Sleep over the water and watch hundreds of scarlet ibis come home at dusk.
X3.trip.bigi-pan.imageCredit: -JvL- from Netherlands, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X3.trip.bigi-pan.label: Bigi Pan (scarlet ibis wetlands, Nickerie)
X3.trip.bigi-pan.value: 68,000 ha estuary reserve north of the Nickerie River, the country's third-largest reserve. Travel the Guianas' 2-day trip: transport from Paramaribo to the Nickerie boat landing, 45-60 min boat to an overwater cabin (air-con, private bathroom with cold water), all meals, sunset scarlet ibis roosting, night caiman spotting and dawn birding with an English-speaking guide.
X3.trip.bigi-pan.limits: Drive time from Paramaribo not on the opened page; not realistic as a day trip. Page does not say if the price is per person. Photo: scarlet ibises in the Jamaer canal near Bigi Pan (2016).

X3.trip.brownsberg.fun: Rainforest mountain, waterfalls, howler monkeys and toucans. Your first proper jungle day.
X3.trip.brownsberg.imageCredit: Andrawaag, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X3.trip.brownsberg.label: Brownsberg Nature Park
X3.trip.brownsberg.value: STINASU-managed park about 130 km south of Paramaribo; the 500 m Brownsberg overlooks the Brokopondo Reservoir. Trails lead to waterfalls; howler monkeys, toucans and about 350 bird species. Lodging, an information centre and a restaurant near the top.
X3.trip.brownsberg.limits: WWF (2012) reported illegal gold mining in the park. Prices from blogs, not operators.

conflicts.value: US$80-130 full-day tour; 2-4 hours' drive each way
US$60-80 day tour; about 2.5 hours

X3.trip.commewijne-bike.fun: Ferry across, rent a bike, pedal past old plantations. Very sundress-and-sunscreen.
X3.trip.commewijne-bike.imageCredit: Ymnes, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X3.trip.commewijne-bike.label: Commewijne plantations by bike
X3.trip.commewijne-bike.value: Cross the river (ferry or the Wijdenbosch Bridge), rent a bike and ride between the old plantations, including Peperpot. About 30-45 minutes by car from Paramaribo, or 30-90 minutes mixing boat and minivan. Guided group tours run about US$40-70 per person.
X3.trip.commewijne-bike.notes: Photo: the Rust en Werk plantation, Commewijne (2022).
X3.trip.commewijne-bike.limits: Prices from travel blogs, not rental shops. No named rental shop found.

conflicts.value: US$5-8/day bike, plus about US$1 ferry
US$5-10 bike rental at Peperpot

X3.trip.dolphins.fun: Sunset boat ride to find dolphins with pink bellies. Peak cute, minimal effort.
X3.trip.dolphins.imageCredit: Amandine Bordin, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X3.trip.dolphins.label: Dolphin spotting at the river mouth (Leonsberg)
X3.trip.dolphins.value: Late-afternoon boat trips from Leonsberg look for Guiana dolphins (Sotalia guianensis, locally 'pink belly dolphins') in the Suriname River estuary, often with the sunset and a stop at Rust en Werk. All-round Tours: EUR 28, 4pm departure, about 3-4 hours, snacks and guide, minimum 3 people, transport to Leonsberg not included. Green Heritage Fund Suriname has studied this population between Leonsberg and Braamspunt since 2005.
X3.trip.dolphins.limits: Sightings are not guaranteed. Prices are operators' listings. Photo shows the same species in French Guiana (2018).

conflicts.value: US$45 per person, 3-hour cruise, 4pm from Leonsberg pier

X3.trip.galibi.fun: Giant leatherbacks laying eggs on the beach. Put February in your calendar.
X3.trip.galibi.imageCredit: JuliasTravels, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X3.trip.galibi.label: Galibi sea turtles (season Feb to Jul/Aug, so not on arrival)
X3.trip.galibi.value: Leatherback and other sea turtles nest on the beach at the Marowijne mouth near the Kalina villages of Christiaankondre and Langamankondre. All-round Tours' 2-day trip: bus via Commewijne to Albina, then boat; turtles come ashore at night depending on the tides; transport, guide, meals and lodging included.
X3.trip.galibi.unit: per person, 2 days all-in (single supplement EUR 50)

sources.publisher: Wikipedia (Galibi, Suriname: Christiaankondre, Langamankondre and Galibi Nature Reserve sections)

X3.trip.galibi.limits: Season dates differ by source; she arrives in late November, outside every quoted window. Photo from 2007.

conflicts.value: mid-February to late July (comments: February to July)
roughly March to August, elsewhere February to August; US$100-150 trip; about 2 hours beyond Albina

X3.trip.jodensavanne.fun: A 2023 UNESCO site, synagogue ruins and a healing spring. Lunch included.
X3.trip.jodensavanne.imageCredit: xiquinhosilva, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X3.trip.jodensavanne.label: Jodensavanne (UNESCO World Heritage, 2023)
X3.trip.jodensavanne.value: Ruins of a 17th-century Sephardi Jewish plantation settlement about 50 km south of Paramaribo on the Suriname River; with Cassipora Creek Cemetery it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in September 2023. All-round Tours' bus day trip goes via Paranam, Redi Doti and Overbridge: synagogue ruins, old graves and a healing spring, with transport, guide, admission, snacks and lunch included.
X3.trip.jodensavanne.limits: Travel time not stated on the tour page. The plantations ran on enslaved labour; the site is a memorial as well as a sight.

X4.church.cathedral.fun: Sunday Mass in a wooden basilica where Peerke Donders is buried. Very you.
X4.church.cathedral.label: Mass at the cathedral
X4.church.cathedral.value: Saint Peter and Paul Cathedral Basilica, Henck Arronstraat 22-24, +597 47 25 21, bisdomparamaribo.org. Listed times: Sunday 10:00am and vigil 7:00pm; weekdays 6:30am and 12:00pm. Peter (Peerke) Donders is buried in the cathedral.
X4.church.cathedral.notes: Phone the parish office to ask about the choir and any English Mass. Photo is under X2.place.cathedral.

X4.community.filipino.fun: Filipino nurses work at AZP. Kabayan are closer than you think.
X4.community.filipino.label: Filipino nurses at AZP
X4.community.filipino.value: Suriname approved recruiting NICU nurses from the Philippines for the Academic Hospital Paramaribo (AZP) in July 2022; by February 2023 they had arrived and were starting work.
X4.community.filipino.notes: Lead: the nurses at AZP and the honorary consul (see life.json K3).
X4.community.filipino.limits: Number not given. No Filipino association, Facebook group or meetup found on an opened page (Philippine DFA pages blocked).

X4.festival.divali.fun: A week of oil lamps on Independence Square. 2027's is yours.
X4.festival.divali.imageCredit: -JvL- from Netherlands, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X4.festival.divali.label: Divali (Festival of Lights)
X4.festival.divali.value: Hindu festival of light; a national holiday since 2010. Oil lamps (diyas) are lit for about a week at Onafhankelijkheidsplein. In 2026 it falls on Sunday 8 November, before her arrival.
X4.festival.divali.limits: The 2027 date is not confirmed by an opened source. Photo: Divali in Paramaribo, 2016.

X4.festival.owru-yari.fun: A two-kilometre firecracker chain on New Year's Eve afternoon. Earplugs recommended.
X4.festival.owru-yari.imageCredit: Ada Korbee, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X4.festival.owru-yari.label: Owru Yari (New Year's Eve), 31 December
X4.festival.owru-yari.value: On the afternoon of 31 December central Paramaribo lights a Pagara Estafette, a firecracker chain about 2 km long, with a marching band; many shops close before noon. Families set off firecrackers shortly before midnight to drive out bad spirits.
X4.festival.owru-yari.notes: Her first big Paramaribo festival, about six weeks after arrival.
X4.festival.owru-yari.limits: Only opened source is a 2018 article. No 2026 programme or fireworks rules found. Photo: Owru Yari from the Readytex balcony, 2016.

X4.festival.phagwa.fun: A colour-powder festival every March. Wear clothes you're happy to sacrifice.
X4.festival.phagwa.label: Holi Phagwa (colour festival), March
X4.festival.phagwa.value: Hindustani spring festival marked with coloured powders, held in March, usually at the Palmentuin or Onafhankelijkheidsplein; it also draws local and foreign visitors.
X4.festival.phagwa.limits: Only opened source is from 2018. The 2027 date (a calendar snippet said 22 March) is unconfirmed, and the Palmentuin may still be closed. No Suriname photo found.

X4.hobby.gym.fun: About SRD 514 a month for a gym. Pom calories, handled.
X4.hobby.gym.label: Gym membership
X4.hobby.gym.value: Average monthly fitness subscription in Paramaribo about EUR 12 (about SRD 514), range about EUR 8.30-18. Hermitage Mall reviews mention a gym there.
X4.hobby.gym.limits: Aggregator estimate (collected in SRD, shown in EUR; observation count not stated). No gym named on an opened page.

X4.hobby.salsa.fun: Suriname has a whole salsa and bachata festival. Next year, you're dancing.
X4.hobby.salsa.label: Salsa and bachata (Salsuri)
X4.hobby.salsa.value: The Salsuri Congress is an annual international salsa and bachata festival in Paramaribo with workshop days, showcases and parties; the 2026 edition is 21-25 October at Theater Thalia (salsuri.net).
X4.hobby.salsa.limits: She arrives after the 2026 edition. No weekly class found; the organiser is the best lead for regular classes.

X4.hobby.yoga.fun: There's been yoga on the Waterkant by the river. Downward dog, river view.
X4.hobby.yoga.label: Yoga
X4.hobby.yoga.value: The Embassy of India's cultural centre (Swami Vivekananda Cultural Centre) runs yoga events; on 14 March 2026 a public International Day of Yoga countdown session was held on the Waterkant by the river.
X4.hobby.yoga.notes: Ask the SVCC whether its classes are open to the public.
X4.hobby.yoga.limits: No regular class schedule, studio or price found on an opened page.

X4.volunteer.green-heritage-fund.fun: Sloths and anteaters need volunteers, and so do their spreadsheets. Your two worlds.
X4.volunteer.green-heritage-fund.label: Volunteering with sloths and anteaters (Green Heritage Fund Suriname)
X4.volunteer.green-heritage-fund.value: Wildlife rescue and rehabilitation group for sloths and anteaters, run largely by volunteers (Surinamese and international, including long-term visitors). Tasks include animal rescue and care, administration, communications, fundraising and event planning; remote help is also welcome. Its dolphin programme takes guests on research trips (max 10 people).
X4.volunteer.green-heritage-fund.limits: Pages undated; current volunteer intake and address not stated.

X5.cute.christmas-store.fun: A Christmas shop open all year. Ber-months forever, basically.
X5.cute.christmas-store.label: The Christmas Store
X5.cute.christmas-store.value: A shop open all year selling holiday decor, gifts and festive items (facebook.com/christmasstoresuriname).

sources.publisher: Surinam Airways, Explore Suriname: 'Shopping: Suriname's Retail Treasures'

X5.cute.christmas-store.limits: Address and hours not on the opened page; undated airline guide.

X5.cute.readytex.fun: Handmade jewellery by local artists. Pretty earrings with a story.
X5.cute.readytex.imageCredit: Ada Korbee, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
X5.cute.readytex.label: Readytex Art Gallery
X5.cute.readytex.value: Shop, studio and art gallery selling handmade jewellery, accessories and clothing by local artists (readytexartgallery.com).

sources.publisher: Surinam Airways, Explore Suriname: 'Shopping: Suriname's Retail Treasures'

X5.cute.readytex.limits: Undated airline guide; hours and prices not found. Photo from 2014.

X5.cute.sweetie-coffee.fun: Tiny family cafe by the palm garden. Iced cappuccino and banana bread.
X5.cute.sweetie-coffee.label: Sweetie Coffee
X5.cute.sweetie-coffee.value: Small family-run cafe next to the Palm Garden, with wooden furniture, greenery and homemade pastries; reviewers single out the iced cappuccino and banana bread. Rated 4.8 from 123 reviews. Open Wed-Sun 10am-6pm, closed Mon-Tue.
X5.cute.sweetie-coffee.limits: Undated aggregator listing; hours may change. A search snippet mentioned limited seating at peak times.

X5.cute.zus-en-zo.fun: Satay on a relaxed terrace. Friday-after-month-end-close energy.
X5.cute.zus-en-zo.label: Zus & Zo
X5.cute.zus-en-zo.value: Near the Palmentuin; known for satay and a relaxed outdoor terrace.
X5.cute.zus-en-zo.limits: One undated guide. No hours or prices.

X5.pretty.cosmetics.fun: Beauty stores at Hermitage, plus Apotheek Suriname for herbal and beauty bits.
X5.pretty.cosmetics.label: Cosmetics and beauty shopping
X5.pretty.cosmetics.value: Hermitage Mall has beauty stores; Apotheek Suriname is listed as a pharmacy and wellness store with herbal remedies and beauty products (apotheeksuriname.com).

sources.publisher: Surinam Airways, Explore Suriname: 'Shopping: Suriname's Retail Treasures'

X5.pretty.cosmetics.limits: No dedicated cosmetics chain named on an opened page; availability of Asian skincare brands unknown.

X5.pretty.facials-spa.fun: Glass facials, foot massages, microneedling. Glow-up options, fully stocked.
X5.pretty.facials-spa.label: Facials, massage and spa treatments
X5.pretty.facials-spa.value: Fresha lists Lux Beauty Clinic (Tammenga; facials and microneedling; 4.8 from 225), Rainha Da Lua Skincare (Rio Negrostraat; 'glass facial'), Divine Serenity Spa (Jourilaan; foot massage) and TheGlowingPod (Radiumstraat).
X5.pretty.facials-spa.limits: Prices use an unlabelled '$'; not recorded. A hotel spa (Torarica) was not confirmed on an opened page.

X5.pretty.hair.fun: One Blauwgrond salon has 929 reviews. That's a lot of happy hair.
X5.pretty.hair.label: Hair salons
X5.pretty.hair.value: Fresha lists highly reviewed hair salons, including Mel An Gi Hair NV (Blauwgrond, 4.9 from 929 reviews), Curl Babes (Andirastraat, 4.9 from 268), Curls and Cuts (Mon Plaisir, 4.9 from 237) and Hair 'n Balance Studio (Blauwgrond, 4.8 from 156).
X5.pretty.hair.limits: Prices on the page use an unlabelled '$'; not recorded. Experience with Asian hair not known.

X5.pretty.nails.fun: Twenty-six salons bookable online. BIAB, chrome, rhinestones: your nails will thrive.
X5.pretty.nails.label: Nail salons
X5.pretty.nails.value: Fresha lists 26 Paramaribo salons for manicures, bookable online, including Delete Beauty Lounge (Frederikastraat 48A, 4.8 from 522 reviews), Ana's Nails Studio (Recifestraat 19, 5.0 from 80), I Do Nails (Jodenbreestraat 52, Centrum), Studio Queens (women only, Granulietstraat) and Sugarcoat (rhinestones, chrome). Scene Beauty Salon SR (Tweede Rijweg) lists a basic manicure at SRD 550 plus SRD 100 for gel, and a luxury manicure at SRD 725.
X5.pretty.nails.limits: Most Fresha prices show only '$', which may be SRD or USD; only Scene Beauty labels SRD. Ratings change. No photo.
